categories.label: Art & Galleries
categories.description: Contemporary art galleries, studios and street art. Programmes move in months rather than weeks, so most of this category is harvested monthly.

categories.label: Churches & Cathedrals
categories.description:
Working churches whose public programme is largely not religious: organ recitals, choral evensong open to anyone, lunchtime concerts, festival performances borrowing the acoustics, heritage openings and civic events.
A category rather than a corner of `music` because these sources do not fit one: the concerts belong to music, the tower tours to museums, the carol services to neither, and the buildings themselves are the reason people come. Bristol's existing church venues had ended up scattered — `music/st-georges-bristol` is a deconsecrated concert hall and belongs where it is — and the point of this file is the ones still in use as churches, which nothing else claimed.

categories.label: Cinema
categories.description: Independent and commercial cinemas, plus film festivals and pop-up screenings.

categories.label: City-wide
categories.description: Cross-category listings sites, the council and the tourist board. These are the safety net: anything the category catalogues miss — pop-ups, one-off community events, venue-less happenings — tends to surface here first.

categories.label: Comedy
categories.description: Comedy clubs, improv, and the venues whose comedy programme is substantial enough to be worth watching on its own.

categories.label: Learning & Talks
categories.description: Public lectures, adult education and outreach — the programmes whose purpose is that someone leaves knowing something. A university publishing its own public programme belongs here rather than among the city-wide aggregators, which is why `education/university-of-bristol` was re-homed out of `citywide`. UWE stays there for now: unlike Bristol's, its entry has real harvest history behind it.

categories.label: Family & Kids
categories.description: City farms, play spaces and companies producing for children. Programmes spike hard in school holidays, which is the main thing to get right here.

categories.label: Festivals
categories.description: Annual, mostly venue-less events. The largest things that happen in the city live here, and almost none of them appear on any venue's website. Announcements cluster in winter and spring for a summer that sells out early.

categories.label: Food & Drink
categories.description: Food halls, breweries and taprooms with public event programmes. Only sources that actually programme events belong here — a restaurant with no events is not a source, however good it is.

categories.label: Gardens & Horticulture
categories.description: Botanic gardens, nurseries, growing projects and open-garden schemes. Sharply seasonal: plant fairs and open days cluster in spring and early summer, and most of this category has nothing on at all in January.

categories.label: Literature & Talks
categories.description: Bookshops with event programmes, literary festivals, spoken word and poetry nights, and public talks.

categories.label: Making & Craft
categories.description:
Makerspaces, workshops, printmaking, woodwork and craft courses.
The distinctive problem in this category is that most listings are *courses*, not events — a ten-week evening class is not the same thing as a one-off workshop, and a "what's on" page is much less useful if it fills up with enrolment listings. Prefer one-off and short workshops, open days and public makes; record a recurring course as `occurrence.kind: recurring` with the pattern stated, rather than as a stream of dated events.

categories.label: Markets
categories.description: Street and indoor markets. Almost all are `occurrence.kind: recurring` — a weekly or monthly pattern rather than dated events — which makes them a good test of that part of the schema.

categories.label: Museums & Heritage
categories.description: Museums, heritage sites and science centres. Mostly permanent collections (`occurrence.kind: ongoing`) punctuated by temporary exhibitions and events.

categories.label: Music
categories.description: Concert halls, grassroots venues, club spaces and the promoters who programme them. Bristol's densest category by volume.

categories.label: Parks & Outdoors
categories.description: Estates, woods and green space that host public events. These are places before they are venues — most of the year they have no programme at all, and then a single weekend brings fifty thousand people.

categories.label: Sport
categories.description: Professional clubs and their grounds. Fixtures are published a season at a time and then move for TV, so the value here is in re-checking dates rather than discovering new events.

categories.label: Theatre
categories.description: Playhouses, studio theatres, circus and physical theatre, and the companies that programme into other people's spaces.

TOUR: Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the

events.summary: Half an hour over four floors of a 1790s merchant's house, told through one household — including the colonial wealth and the trafficking of enslaved Africans that paid for it. Runs Friday to Sunday, so it covers most of the long weekend.
events.description:
Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the history of
the house and the people who lived there.

Through the lens of a single household, guests will learn, not only about day-to-day life
in Georgian times, but about the dramatic and harrowing global events which fuelled an era
of both prosperity and tragedy, technology and romance, tradition and progress.

Tours are approximately 30 minutes long. Visitors will be taken on a brief historical
journey throughout four floors of the 230 year old Georgian town house. You can book a
tour online up to two days before the event; box office tickets may be available to buy on
the day (subject to availability). Please arrive no more than five minutes early to avoid
having to wait around outside.

Eating and drinking (with the exception of bottled water) is not permitted inside the
museum.

Be aware that the tour deals with more difficult themes relating to the house’s colonial
past and involvement with the trafficking of enslaved Africans which some visitors may
find distressing.

**Accessibility.** The number of stairs in the museum mean that the tour is not accessible
for those with reduced mobility. **Facilities.** There is no access to toilet facilities on
premises.

**Book tickets.** Standard ticket: £5. Under 16s ticket: Free. Carer/sighted guide ticket:
Free.

Tours start: Fridays – 11:30am and 2pm; Saturdays – 11:30am and 2pm; Sundays – 11:30am and
2pm. You can book online up to two days before the event, box office tickets may be
available to buy on the day (subject to availability).

events.title: John Wesley and Mindfulness Museum Display
events.venueName: The New Room / John Wesley's Chapel
events.raw:
"Good health of both body and mind for all." — John Wesley

John Wesley believed that it was mind, body, and soul that gave somebody
good health. Following this holistic approach would lead to living a happy
life.…

8th April, 2026 onwards. Free with normal Museum admission.
events.summary:
A small display drawn from the New Room's collection and archive on Wesley's
interest in medicine and natural remedies — he ran a free dispensary here,
and when the money ran out wrote a self-help medical guide that stayed a
bestseller for a century. Included in museum admission.
events.description:
"Good health of both body and mind for all." John Wesley

John Wesley believed that it was mind, body, and soul that gave somebody
good health. Following this holistic approach would lead to living a happy
life.

John was interested in medicine and natural remedies. At The New Room, he
created a dispensary of free medical care. When John ran out of money to
continue this, he wrote a self-help guide to medicine. The Primitive Physic:
or an Easy and Natural Method of Curing Most Diseases was published in
Bristol in 1747 and became a bestseller for a century.

Explore items from the John Wesley's New Room collection and archive linked
to health and wellbeing.

8th April, 2026 onwards.

Free with normal Museum admission.

**Visit Our Museum**

The Museum at the New Room tells the incredible history of John and Charles
Wesley, the early beginnings of Methodism and its relevance today. The
museum is housed in the original 1748 rooms.

Discover how the New Room played a vital role in providing healthcare and
education for those in need. Discover the challenges faced by Wesley in his
fight for social justice and be inspired to continue that work today.

Your ticket entitles you to 12 months free entry to the museum.

This is part of the Care & Repair Festival, organised by Sparks, John
Wesley's New Room, and Bristol BID. The Care & Repair Festival is a joyful,
family-friendly celebration of making, mending, and creativity, taking place
from 7-19 April 2026.

events.description:
Unearth the stories, mishaps and mayhem behind Brunel’s legacy, and discover how the city
of Bristol helped to forge one of history’s greatest engineers.

Covering just over 3 miles of the harbourside, the tours last approximately 2 hrs 15 mins
and commence and finish outside The Board Walk restaurant in Brunel Square - located just
outside the main entrance to Bristol Dockyards.

Primarily following a circular route around Bristol’s Floating Harbour, Mr. Brunel will
discuss his Bristol born projects, tales from his own life, the history of the harbour as
well as some interesting chapters from Bristol’s past and present. Main stops on the tour
include Underfall Yard, Cumberland Basin, Queen Square and of course, the SS Great
Britain.

events.title: Folly
events.raw:
**Folly** — 23 June - 30 August 2026. Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road,
Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free. Tuesday - Sunday: 10am - 5pm (Closed
Mondays).
events.summary: Four RWA Academicians, curated by Peter Burke, on folly in every sense: the ornamental towers and mock ruins of the eighteenth century, the obsolete monuments of modern ideology, and the private project pursued against all logic. Free, and in its final fortnight.
events.description:
Curated by Peter Burke RWA, with works by Peter Burke RWA, Judith Jones
RWA, Jemma Gunning RWA RE and Karl Singporewala RWA RIBA.

The exhibition explores folly through several lenses. It looks at the
tradition of folly building that emerged centuries ago in Britain,
where wealthy individuals chose to demonstrate their prosperity by
commissioning ornamental structures, often as towers or mock ruins. It
asks whether modern structures shaped by political, religious or
commercial ideologies, now redundant or obsolete, constitute
contemporary follies. And it explores the urge to undertake an
idiosyncratic project for its own sake, flying in the face of logic.

Across a wide range of mediums, these themes run as a common thread for
contemporary artistic exploration.

Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road, Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free.
Tuesday – Sunday: 10am – 5pm, closed Mondays.

events.title: Polly Braden: Against the Tide
events.raw:
**Exhibitions** — 27 June - 27 September 2026, 11:00 - 18:00.
Ground floor galleries. FREE, donations welcome.

Polly Braden: Against the Tide — *An exhibition by documentary
photographer Polly Braden in collaboration with young people in coastal
towns across England.*
events.summary: Documentary portraits and testimony from 16–25-year-olds in nine coastal towns, made with Polly Braden over a year for the Guardian's Seascape series. Free, ground floor.
events.description:
This summer, Arnolfini presents *Against the Tide*, a new exhibition by
documentary photographer Polly Braden, created in collaboration with
young people growing up in some of the most deprived and often
forgotten places across England.

Known for her intimate, long-term collaborations, Polly Braden's work
focuses on overlooked communities and social issues, and her
distinctive style combines quiet observation with deep empathy.

*Against the Tide* is a project led by Braden in collaboration with
journalist Lisa Bachelor as part of *The Guardian*'s Seascape series.
The pair have spent more than a year visiting coastal locations,
talking to young people about their lives and what matters to them. The
result is a layered picture of coastal England today that goes beyond
the usual, negative portrayals and which shines a light on the hope
that is sometimes hidden from public view.

Across intimate portraits and first-hand testimony, *Against the Tide*
brings audiences face-to-face with a generation navigating life at the
sharp edge of inequality, while also imagining something different.
Alongside accounts of isolation and lack of opportunity are expressions
of resilience, ambition and hope, and a clear message: coastal towns
are not just sites of decline, but places of creativity and
possibility.

Spanning places that include Weston-super-Mare, Scarborough, Grimsby,
Southend, Portsmouth, Whitehaven, Tendring, Rhyl and Blackpool, the
work reveals a side of coastal Britain rarely seen in national
narratives. It was developed over a year through sustained
collaboration with 16–25-year-olds across these towns.

Supported by Arts Council England, the Guardian's Seascape series, the
University of Lancaster and UCL.

events.title: Jonathan Baldock: Held
events.raw:
**Exhibitions** — 27 June - 27 September 2026, 11:00 - 18:00.
First floor galleries. FREE, (donations welcome).

Jonathan Baldock: Held — *Arnolfini transforms into a colourful,
immersive wilderness of nature and folklore this summer.*
events.summary: Baldock's ceramics, textiles and sound turn the first floor into a folkloric garden, built around a monumental wild bear commissioned for the show and made to be held. Free, and up all bank holiday weekend.
events.description:
Known for his striking installations, Jonathan Baldock combines
ceramics, textiles and sound to create environments that are both
playful and thought-provoking. His work draws on folklore, traditional
craft and personal history, shaped by skills passed down through
generations of making.

*Held* features a monumental wild bear sculpture, commissioned by
Arnolfini. It invites visitors into a direct physical encounter — not
to be held, but to hold us.

> "The English artist has created a tense world of folkloric
> psychedelia and pagan aesthetics that is weird, threatening — and
> utterly compelling" — Eddy Frankel, *The Guardian* (5-star review)

At Arnolfini, the galleries become a colourful, sensory landscape
inspired by the natural world, somewhere between a garden and a
wilderness. *Aether* — a work formed from beeswax, ceramic and glass —
hovers overhead, evoking a space between worlds. At the entrance,
visitors are welcomed by *The Caretakers*, ceremonial costumes adorned
with hand-stitched plant motifs, setting the tone for a space rooted in
care. Beyond, a vivid array of ceramic and wall-based textile
sculptures unfolds: flowers with faces emerging from petals, trailing
roots and body parts, creating a cultivated wilderness that blurs
boundaries between the human and the natural.

Sound by artist Luke Barton and a custom scent by Lora Hemy fill the
space, adding to the exhibition's immersive and intimate atmosphere.

The bear itself draws on a long cultural history, from ancient myth to
the familiar comfort of childhood toys. Over the course of the
exhibition, its surface will become worn through use, carrying the
marks of the thousands of people who encounter it. Its face, modelled
on a scan of the artist's mother, adds a deeply personal dimension.

In an age increasingly defined by loneliness, accelerated by the rise
of AI and a gradual loss of communal spaces, *Held* proposes physical
closeness as a radical and necessary gesture.

This exhibition has been generously supported by the Henry Moore
Foundation. A monograph published to coincide with the show is
available from the Arnolfini Bookshop.

events.title: If Schools Were Ours to Imagine
events.raw:
When: 1 Jul 2026 – 2 Jan 2027
Where: Open City Lab
Recommended for: Families

Head to our Open City Lab, get creative and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how
schools could be made fairer for everyone.
events.summary: An exhibition that visitors add to as they go, collecting ideas about what a fairer school would look like. In the Open City Lab until January.
events.description:
What would it look like if we could decide what schools were like in future? Get creative
and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how schools could be made fairer for everyone.

There are six mini-activities in the space:

- Head to the retro desks and smell, touch, and listen to connect with local Bristolian's
  memories of school.
- It's school dance time. Express how people's stories of school make you feel through
  movement.
- Make a clay model of what would you add to school to make it better (fairer)?
- If you could do anything on your dream school day, what would it be? Decorate a piece of
  bunting to add to the display.
- Share your thoughts and reflections on what you've experienced in the space, and your own
  school stories. Write it down or record it with the team.
- Explore an interactive map of Bristol with stories from the repair-ed archive.

This project is in partnership with Reparative Futures of Education (Repair-Ed) from the
University of Oxford. This collaboration builds on the team's existing work which explores
people's experiences of schooling in relation to racial and class inequality in Bristol and
how schools could be made fairer in future.

**Access considerations** — This activity takes place in a slightly enclosed ground floor
space that is wheelchair accessible with a lot of room between tables and information stands.

events.title: 1000 Years of Fashion History – an exhibition in miniature

price.text: Free, donations welcome. Drop in, no booking necessary.

events.raw:
18 July—1 November 2026

EXHIBITION: A timeline in miniature, with more than 100 hand-made costumes modelled by
fashion dolls.
events.summary: More than a hundred hand-made period costumes on twelve-inch dolls, Saxon to the 1980s, made over six years by Lisa Jayne Smith while she was being treated for breast cancer. Open across the weekend, free.
events.description:
From Saxon robes to Elizabethan ruffs, Victorian tartan and punk piercings, come and see
how what we wear has changed across time… in miniature!

This exhibition has been created by Lisa Jayne Smith, following a career working in theatre
and running her own business making and adapting period costume.

She has been an avid fan of costume history for as long as she can remember, and the
exhibition is inspired by a book she came across while costuming for a play, ‘The Change in
Fashion from 1066-1960s’.

Lisa spent six years researching and making more than 100 miniature historical costumes
while receiving treatment for breast cancer.

Each hand made outfit, modelled by a 12-inch fashion doll, is complete down to the tiniest
detail. The amount of time spent on each model would depend on the size and era of each
costume, anything from a week to a month.

Journey through time, from the Saxons through Medieval, Renaissance, Tudor, Elizabethan,
Jacobean, Carolean, Restoration, Stuart, Georgian, Victorian, Edwardian, 1910’s, 1920’s,
1930’s, 1940’s, 1950’s, 1960’s, 1970’s up to the 1980’s.

"I hope you enjoy looking at them as much as I have in making and creating them!" — Lisa
Jayne Smith

**Booking information.** This exhibition is located in the first floor costume gallery,
please be aware there are only stairs to this floor, no lift is available. Suitable for
children of all ages. Drop in, no booking necessary. Free, donations welcome.

events.raw:
Conservation Carnival! — 18 July – 31 August

Celebrate the incredible conservation success stories helping to protect our oceans and
wildlife this summer at Bristol Aquarium.

Join us for **Conservation Carnival**, where you’ll discover inspiring stories of species
recovery, habitat restoration and the amazing work of conservation charities making a real
difference around the world. Through interactive activities, guided tours and
family-friendly experiences, you’ll learn how small actions can help protect our blue
planet.

**Activities**

- **Take on the Conservation Trail** — Collect stamps as you journey through the aquarium,
  discovering six fascinating species and the conservation projects helping them thrive.
- **Daily Save Our Seas Guided Tours – 11am** — Join our expert team each day for a free
  guided conservation tour through a different area of the aquarium. Tours last
  approximately 15–20 minutes and include time for questions.
- **Treasure or Trash: Sandpit Search – Daily at 4pm** — Become a marine explorer as you
  dig through our interactive beach combing sandpit. Discover shark teeth, shark egg
  cases, fossils, seashells, coral fragments and ancient marine specimens. You’ll also
  uncover examples of plastic pollution and learn why keeping our beaches clean is so
  important for marine wildlife.
- **Visit the Conservation Corner** — Beach clean information, conservation charities you
  can support, how Bristol Aquarium and Aspro Parks help protect wildlife, and children’s
  colouring activities.

All Conservation Carnival activities are included with standard aquarium admission.

events.summary: Interactive games threaded through the ship and dockyard — jar fishing, a giant skipping rope, orders shouted down the speaking trumpets — all drawn from real voyages. Included with admission and running right through the bank holiday weekend.
events.description:
Pack up your playmates and set sail for fun.

This summer at Bristol Dockyards – home of SS Great Britain – we're bringing the stories
of one of the world's most extraordinary ships to life through games, challenges and a
whole lot of laughs.

From the dockside to the dining room, take part in interactive challenges inspired by the
SS Great Britain’s global voyages. Here’s a taste of what’s in store:

- **Jar Fishing:** Child passengers would dangle jars into the sea to catch fish –
  without even being able to see what they'd caught! Now it's your turn.
- **Jump Rope:** Swing into action with our giant jump rope – a favourite from the
  streets of New York City. How long can you keep going?
- **Good Shout:** Head down to the engine room and listen out for your orders – called
  out through the speaking trumpets just like the real crew. How many commands can you
  get right?
- **Who Made All the Pies?** Race to make three fruit pies in the ship’s galley before
  anyone else! Flip cards to build your desserts, based on a real menu from 1863.

Key info — Time: 10:00am-5:00pm. Price: Included in your ticket.

**Kids Go Free - all summer long.** One child free for every paying adult – from now
until 2 September. Come back as many times as you like at no extra cost: One ticket, a
whole year of adventures.

events.description:
This summer we've got three fun activities in the kitchen, all delving into food chemistry
and how we can eat sustainably.

Learn a bit more about what our food is made of and some of the hidden chemistry that goes
in to cooking, have a fun tasting experience and learn some new foody skills to try at home!

**Activities on offer:**

- **The Big Green Grill-Off** — Love a BBQ? Not sure about all the meat? Become a
  sustainable chef as you invent and cook your own meat-free burgers.
- **Supercool Sorbet** — How can salt help things freeze? Use some clever chemistry to make
  sorbet in minutes.
- **Will it Mix?** — We've heard that oil and water don't mix but, with a bit of science, we
  reckon they might. It's time to get saucy – and make some mayonnaise!

Activities running will vary depending on term time verses weekends and holidays. Please
always check the activity screens on arrival to see which activities are running at what
time each day.

**Accessibility / allergens** — This activity takes place on a raised kitchen counter. When
the venue is busy, you may need to share space and equipment with other visitors. Allergens
include milk, eggs and gluten though the activity can be adapted. Please speak to a member
of staff about any allergies before taking part.

events.title: Besides the Sea
events.raw:
**Besides the Sea** — 01 August - 25 October 2026, 11:00 - 18:00.

*What does living in Weston, and in similar coastal towns, mean for
young people trying to build creative lives today?*
events.summary: Six young photographers from Bristol and Weston on place, identity and growing up by the sea, with a collaborative poem by Beth Calverley. A companion piece to Against the Tide.
events.description:
*Besides the Sea* celebrates the many ways creativity shapes life in
Weston: how it brings people together, enriches everyday experiences,
amplifies new voices and helps us imagine new possibilities.

The exhibition brings together work by six young artists based in
Bristol and Weston. The work was developed through workshops led by
artist Jamie Dormer-Durling, connected to *Against the Tide* (27 June –
27 September 2026), a project developed by photographer Polly Braden in
collaboration with journalist Lisa Bachelor for *The Guardian*'s
Seascape series.

Inside the gallery, photographs by Bayan Alahmad, Archie Byron, Braden
Evans, Siobhan Evans, Jess May Long and Will Shergold explore place,
identity and creativity through their personal experiences of growing
up in Weston. Their work weaves together everyday moments, memories,
dreams and nostalgia, the textures of the natural environment, and the
rhythms of working-class culture — revealing the quiet beauty found
within Weston's streets, shorelines and communities. The exhibition
also features a collaborative poem written by the young people with
poet Beth Calverley.

Along the corridor walls, Weston's creative landscape — nurtured over
the years by residents and organisations such as Super Culture and
Common Waves CIC — unfolds through vibrant snapshots of gatherings,
public artworks and interventions, with Calverley's words woven
throughout.

Once a small fishing village, then a Victorian seaside resort, and now
a regenerated coastal town with a growing arts scene, Weston provides
the backdrop for this exploration of how creativity can shape a place
and the people who call it home.

break: 1 – 1.30pm).
events.summary: Stuart Cranfield's four-Saturday introduction to drawing the figure — proportion, tone, line, then longer poses. The final session falls on Saturday 29 August, and single sessions can be booked.
events.description:
Ever wanted to build confidence in life drawing? This informal
four-week course with artist Stuart Cranfield offers a welcoming
introduction to the fundamentals of drawing the figure. Through
practical exercises and guided tuition, you'll develop the core skills
needed to approach life drawing with greater confidence and
understanding.

Each session focuses on a different aspect of foundational life
drawing, with a maximum of 20 participants to allow for individual
attention and a supportive learning environment. The sessions take
place in the new Light Studio on the second floor.

Across the four sessions we cover:

- **Proportion** — methods for constructing a drawing and understanding
  the figure's underlying structure.
- **Tone** — ways of simplifying form and capturing light and shadow,
  and exploring colour.
- **Line** — exploring the language, quality and expressive potential
  of line.
- **Putting it together** — an opportunity to bring these elements
  together through longer poses, with more one-to-one support.

All materials are provided. Book all four sessions for £120 (click on
the 8th August and select the full series ticket); individual sessions
are £35.

*Journey 3.0* is a joint exhibition showcasing collaborative and
independent works by artists Anna Perra and Tony Church.

Since 2021 the two have developed an artistic partnership exploring
abstract and expressive painting through an intuitive dialogue between
shape, form, colour and movement. Their paintings are bold
compositions with energetic mark-making and vibrant colour palettes,

gestures.

charitable initiatives through their creative practice. While each

unique exchange of ideas, perspectives and processes.

events.summary: Five ranger- and volunteer-led walks marking a century of public ownership, each on a different theme — archaeology, wildlife, Repton's landscape, the churchyard and areas normally closed off.
events.description:
A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and celebrate 100
years of public ownership.

Each walk focuses on an aspect of the estate's rich wildlife, its historical
connections or its archaeological discoveries. Walk leaders will take you for a gentle
stroll to different parts of the park sharing what makes the Blaise Estate so special.

**Hidden Blaise** — Join the estate rangers for a guided tour around the estate and
visit areas usually closed to the public. Dates: Sunday 25 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**Blaise Community Garden** — A guided tour around the Community Garden to learn about
the history of the site and how its changed over the years. If you want to discover
how a thriving community garden works then this is the tour for you! Dates: Saturday 15
August, Saturday 19 September. Times: 2pm to 3pm.

**Archaeology and wildlife** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and the Bristol
Regional Environmental Records Centre (BRERC) to find out more about Blaise's
archaeological discoveries and rich wildlife. Dates: Thursday 10 September. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

**Humphrey Repton's landscape** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and explore the
picturesque parkland created for the Harford Family by the famous landscape designer
Humphrey Repton. Dates: Thursday 8 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**St Mary's Church and churchyard** — A guided walk exploring St Mary's church and
churchyard. Learn about the history of this amazing space, the historic memorials and
its links to Bristol's merchant history. Dates: Thursday 22 October. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

All walks last around 90 minutes and start from Blaise Museum unless otherwise stated.
Please arrive at least five minutes before the start of the walk. Suitable outdoor
clothing and a bottle of water are recommended. This event may have to be cancelled at
short notice due external factors such as weather conditions. Tours will go ahead in
wet weather unless the conditions are extreme. Well behaved dogs on leads are only
permitted on walks that specify this in the information above.

Free, donations welcome. Booking essential.

events.title: Bristol's Grenfell Memorial Panel
events.raw:
Bristol Cathedral is honoured to display Bristol Star Stitchers'
contribution to the Grenfell Memorial Quilt, a moving tribute to all those
affected by the Grenfell Tower disaster.

Bristol Star Stitchers have created a 12ft x 12ft panel honours the 72
people who died in the fire on 14 June 2017, as well as those who survived,
were injured, or lost their homes. It forms part of a nationwide memorial
project inspired by a call from relatives and friends of those affected,
with around 90 panels created by groups across the UK ahead of the
disaster's tenth anniversary in 2027.

The Bristol panel is also a story of community. Made from recycled fabrics
collected from charity shops and other sources, it brought together more
than 30 people of all ages and levels of sewing experience. What began as
small gatherings in people's homes grew into a shared endeavour at the
Vassall Community Hub in Fishponds, where friendships were formed and
skills, stories and countless hours were shared.

At the heart of the panel are 72 embroidered stars, each bearing the name
and age of a person who died. Families and loved ones are stitched close
together, reflecting the lives, relationships and communities behind the
headlines. Flowers and foliage symbolise hope and renewal, while the tower
itself stands as a reminder that those affected must not be forgotten.

Visitors are warmly invited to spend time with this remarkable artwork,
remember those who were lost, and reflect on the power of communities
coming together in solidarity.

Free admission. All welcome.

Mon 17 Aug | 10:00 - 16:00
events.summary:
Bristol's twelve-foot panel for the national Grenfell Memorial Quilt, on
free display in the cathedral until mid-September. Stitched by more than
thirty people from recycled charity-shop fabric, it carries 72 embroidered
stars, one for each person who died.

events.description:
A creativity-led summer holiday club for children aged 5 to 8.

A joyful week of open-ended art, creative play and outdoor atelier
practice, designed to build confidence, community and connection.

At Mini Atelier School, children will explore open-ended art,
creative play and experimental making through daily Open Studio
sessions.

They will also take part in expert-led visual arts workshops with
Let's Make Art, exploring themes inspired by the natural world. Each
day includes Outdoor Atelier time, where children take their creative
practice outside.

To close the week, families are invited to a Friday exhibition
celebrating the children's work, ideas and creative process.

- Ages – 5 to 8 years
- Times – 10am to 4pm
- Early drop-off – From 9am, £5 per day
- Late pick-up – Until 5pm, £6 per day, Monday to Thursday only
- Location – The Mill Room, St Anne's House, St Anne's Road,
  Brislington, Bristol, BS4 4AB
- Capacity – 23 places total
- Staff ratio – 1:8
- 5-day programme – £250, Monday to Friday
- 3-day programme – £150, Tuesday to Thursday

There is no late pick-up on Friday, as families are invited to the
final exhibition from 4pm to 5pm.

What children will gain:

**Creative skills** — Painting, printmaking, collage, clay,
photography and sculpture.

**Time to go deeper** — Space to develop larger-scale creative
projects across the week.

**Community and confidence** — Opportunities to work alongside other
children, share ideas and build connection.

**Nature-led inspiration** — Daily time outside, using the natural
world to inform the creative process.

**Pride and ownership** — Children will help prepare the final Friday
exhibition and share their work with families.

Have you ever thought that moths are just drab butterflies? That the only thing
they do is eat holes in your clothes? This 2-part crash course in moths will
prove you wrong!

they differ from butterflies, why they matter ecologically, and how to set a
trap.

Part two, in person at Grow Wilder, Thursday 20 August, 9:00am–10:30am:
examining what the trap caught overnight and identifying the species found.

between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome.

Come along to our new weekly summer sessions at Grow Wilder to experience some
of the wonderful wildlife found at our urban nature reserve!

In this session we'll be carrying out a bioblitz at Green Shoots, spreading out
to discover and record as much wildlife as we can! We'll be looking at insects,
plants, birds, reptiles and checking for any signs of mammals too — and we'll
discuss why bioblitzes are so useful.

This will be an active session in an outdoor space, and will take place no
matter the weather — so dress for the weather!

This event is suitable for young people from any level of knowledge or
experience! Come along and say hello, meet new people and learn a new skill.

Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL — reachable on Metrobus
M1, M3 or M4 from the city centre. Parents and siblings are also welcome.

events.timesText: 19:00-23:00; beginner lessons run until roughly 21:30, then merge with the general jam
events.summary: A rope-tying jam built around skill-sharing, with two suspension points and experienced people on hand. A separate beginners' tuition ticket covers fundamental harnesses and transitions; for August they strongly recommend bringing a partner, and require one for the lesson.
events.description:
A welcoming event focused on connection, creativity, and skill-sharing.
Two ticket options: **Jam only** and **Jam + Tuition**.

The jam gives space for self-led tying, collaborative exploration, or
learning through observation and exchange, with 2 suspension points
available and support from more experienced folk in the room.

The tuition is aimed at absolute beginners who have never touched rope
before, and at those with some experience who want to refine their
foundations. Teaching covers fundamental harnesses, transitions
(linking ties together), and building confidence and flow.

For August's session the organisers strongly recommend attending with a
partner, and consider it a requirement for anyone wishing to take part
in the lesson. Beginner lessons run until roughly 9:30pm, at which
point they merge with the general jam.

Snacks, water, tea and coffee and communal rope are provided.

events.description:
Rest under a shady tree and take up your pencils! On Thursday 20th August,
come down to the University of Bristol Botanic Garden for an evening of
sketching and creatively exploring some of the city's long-lived trees.

events.title: FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION POETRY NIGHT
events.raw:
**FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION POETRY NIGHT** — Thursday
20 August 2026, doors 18:30, performances from 19:30. Free with an
optional donation; all proceeds to Dandelion-DIY. Headliners Aish
Humphreys and Edson Burton, hosted by Tom Denbigh, with an open mic.
The event page's own copy reads "Thursday 21st August", which is a
Friday — the listing date of Thursday 20 August is what I have taken.
events.summary: The closing night of the Folk House's queer art exhibition — two headline poets, Aish Humphreys and Edson Burton, an open mic, and donations going to Dandelion-DIY.
events.description:
**FOLKHOUSE PRIDE EXHIBITION: A CELEBRATION | Thursday 21st August
Doors: 6:30pm Performances from 7:30pm**

Join us for a night of flowing words and crafted lyricism as we bring
the Folkhouse Summer Queer Art exhibition to a close.

Featuring two headliners — the impeccable **Aish Humphreys** and the
inimitable **Edson Burton** — expect a night of queer poetry
surrounded by the brilliant artwork featured in our Pride open call,
and of course an open mic with an warm invitation to get involved.

The celebration will be hosted by notoriously queer poet Tom Denbigh,
tickets are free, with an option to donate, and all proceeds will go
directly to Dandelion-DIY. A little more about our headliners:

**Aish Humpries**

Aish is a poet, theatre maker and host from Cornwall, living in
Bristol. He is a host at Satellite of Love, a co-producer of the queer
poetry special for Lyra Festival and was a Young Curator with MAYK for
Mayfest 2024.

His first poetry pamphlet, Saints of Golden Hour was released in
February 2023 which explores soberness, girlhood, queer relationships
and the gods we create for ourselves. He is currently collaborating on
the production of the spoken word theatre show, Girlhood in T which
explores transness, masculinity and friendship.

**Edson Burton**

Dr Edson Burton is a prolific writer of audio, live drama and poetry.

Edson won the 2025 Tinniswood Prize for Man Friday an adaption of
Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe.

His previous audio dramas include the acclaimed R4 series Deacon
starring Don Warrington.

Recent live work includes the listening journey _Duppy Hunter_
produced by Tamasha Theatre, and the theatrical promenade Destination
Old Market

He is the author of the poetry collections, Seasoned and Witness.

He is a member of Writers Mosaic the film collective Come the
Revolution, a board member of Lyra poetry festival and Afrika Eye film
festival.

events.summary: A free facilitated space to sit with feelings about climate change alongside neighbours — no advice given, no action expected, and listening is enough.
events.description:
With the recent heatwaves many local people have been feeling the
impacts of climate change on their everyday life. Come together with
neighbours to reflect and share feelings about climate change in a
caring and considerate space.

Questions about the event can be emailed to: futuremancy@gmail.com

Not sure what a Climate Cafe is? We liked this quick explainer from
the Climate Psychology Alliance of North America:
https://www.climatepsychology.us/climate-cafes/.

This is a space that is designed for us to reflect on our feelings
about the changing climate, which can often be difficult to access.
As such, you don't have to do anything, and you won't be expected to
sign up to any action or activity, unless that feels supportive to
you. You can just listen. No-one will be giving advice, and no
emotional response is 'wrong'. We are not trying to minimise, change
or 'look on the bright side' of any reaction you might have. We are
expressing these feelings together.

events.title: Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club: In The Best Interests of Children
events.raw:
**Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club: In The Best Interests of
Children** — Saturday 22 August 2026, 12:00–14:00, £5. A
family-friendly screening of the 1977 documentary by Elizabeth
Stevens, Cathy Zheutlin and Frances Reid, presented with Reverie
Cineclub.
events.summary: A rarely screened 1977 documentary following lesbian mothers fighting for custody of their children, made to educate family court judges and now a landmark of queer family history — with tea and talk afterwards.
events.description:
Friendly Neighbourhood Film Club and Reverie Cineclub present a
family-friendly screening of IN THE BEST INTERESTS OF THE CHILDREN
(1977), the groundbreaking documentary by Elizabeth Stevens, Cathy
Zheutlin and Frances Reid following lesbian mothers fighting for the
right to custody of their children.

Rarely screened for many years, this remarkable and underseen
documentary offers an intimate portrait of eight families. Giving
equal space to mothers and their children, the film captures their
experiences of family, upbringing and queer parenthood with warmth
and raw honesty. Originally produced to educate family court judges,
it has since become an important document of LGBTQ+ family history
and feminist filmmaking.

Made at a time when lesbian mothers routinely lost custody of their
children because of their sexuality, the film documents the legal and
social challenges these families faced while centering their
experiences of love and community. Through candid interviews and
snapshots of everyday life, the film reveals both the realities of
discrimination, and the strength, dignity and joy of queer families.

We chose this film because of the care with which it approaches its
subjects. While some laws and societal attitudes have changed since
the film was made, LGBTQ+ people continue to face barriers and public
debate around family life and parenthood. IN THE BEST INTERESTS OF
THE CHILDREN remains a timely reminder of why these stories matter.

After the screening, there will be space to stay, chat and reflect
together over tea and coffee. Whether you're discovering the film for
the first time or revisiting this landmark of queer cinema, everyone
is welcome.

events.raw: **Event 24/08: Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi introduces The Ghost of the Mountains** — From £6.00.
events.summary: Conservation scientist Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi on twenty years tracking snow leopards in the high Himalaya, and the book that came out of it.
events.description:
**We are absolutely thrilled to welcome the award-winning scientist and conservationist, Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi, to discuss his debut novel, *The Ghost of the Mountains: Unravelling the Secrets of the Snow Leopard*. The Ghost of the Mountains is a story of discovery, conservation and adventure on the trail of one of the most elusive and mysterious predators, brought to life by the world-leading expert on snow leopards.**

**Date:**
Monday 24th of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£20 ticket with *The Ghost of the Mountains* (hardback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***The Ghost of the Mountain: Unravelling the Secrets of the Snow Leopard***

Silent, solitary and beautiful: snow leopards inhabit the cliffs and rugged mountains of central Asia at heights of over 3,000 metres. Thickly furred, with silver-grey pelts, they are so well camouflaged that they vanish into the rocky landscape.

For twenty years, scientist and mountaineer Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi– known as Kullu– has studied the snow leopard in the highest reaches of the Himalaya. The snow leopard is the most elusive of cats.

With their silver-grey pelts and long tails, they move silently through glaciers, snow, rocks and the icy peaks of their wild, mountainous habitat. Rarely seen, they are often regarded as mythical, but this is an animal that faces extraordinary daily challenges, and whose survival depends on the delicate balance of climate, prey, landscape and local people.

Living for months at a time in some of the most difficult-to-reach places on earth, Kullu has pioneered research that shines fresh light on these charismatic and vulnerable animals. His work makes a compelling and urgent case for their conservation.

Combining scientific authority, high-altitude fieldwork and powerful storytelling, *The Ghost of the Mountains* is a gripping exploration into what it takes to save the snow leopard.

*‘A brave, unique field-study of the most extraordinary cat on the planet - the Snow*
*Leopard - elusive, Spartan and beautiful’ Desmond Morris*

*‘Enchanting. The author is a most amiable guide on the mountainside, and this deeply*
*informed book gave me hope for the future of conservation’ Sara Wheeler*

*'Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi has spent his adult life studying, following and trying to protect snow leopards. The Ghost of the Mountains takes readers into the field, high in the Himalayas. The story it tells is by turns beautiful, terrible, and encouraging’ Elizabeth Kolbert*

*‘What a thrilling and intrepid story. Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi takes us into the icy heights of the Himalaya, tracking the elusive snow leopard and bringing to life both this solitary animal and the threatened world it inhabits. Beautifully told, it's a tale of beauty, drama and wild landscapes but also one of the entangled lives of snow leopards, their prey and the humans who share their terrain’ Andrea Wulf*

*‘Marvellous - quite literally. A thrilling story of adventure amongst high mountains, deep mysteries, elusive animals and vertiginous facts’ Charles Foster*

***ABOUT THE AUTHOR***

**Dr Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi** is an award-winning scientist and conservationist who has studied the snow leopard for twenty years. A Fellow of the British Ecological Society, he is a scientist with the Nature Conservation Foundation, a National NGO in India, and the Country Director for the Snow Leopard Trust, an international NGO. His field research is concentrated in India, Nepal, Kyrgyzstan and Mongolia. *The Ghost of the Mountains* is his first book.

events.raw:
**Poetry Peace Feast** — Tuesday 25 August 2026, 19:00–21:00. £15
adults / £7.50 children, with "Pay it Forward" tickets. Bridges for
Communities present an evening of storytelling, conversation and
poetry with Bristol Poet Laureate Sukina Noor and restorative poet

events.summary: Bridges for Communities bring their peace feast back to the Folk House — a shared meal with Bristol Poet Laureate Sukina Noor and Leeza Awojobi, built around the question of how you sustain a village.
events.description:
We're returning to Bristol Folk House! Join us for an evening of
storytelling, conversation and poetry featuring Bristol Poet Laureate
Sukina Noor and restorative poet Leeza Awojobi. This is invitation to
share in food which nourishes the body and soul, exchange meaningful
ideas and leave feeling energised for the wellbeing of your community.

At Bridges for Communities, we love all things collective and have
recently been thinking about the phrase 'It takes a Village'. We know
it takes a village, but how to sustain one? This peace feast builds on
a conversation we've been having in a more creative way. It explores
the complex tension between the needs of the individual and the
collective. It brings together storytelling and collaboration in a way
which suggests rather than dictates, opening up fresh pathways for
engaging across difference. For those feeling extra bold, come
prepared to share your thoughts in an informal guided activity.

Peace Feasts bring people together around a meal, to listen to music,
exchange stories and hear from guest speakers. They celebrate local
communities, help us to see the world through someone else's eyes, and
create spaces for friendships to grow between people from different
backgrounds and experiences of life.

events.title: Introduction to Conservation (3-day course) for 16-30 yr olds
events.raw:
**Introduction to Conservation (3-day course) for 16-30 yr olds** — Wednesday 26
August 2026 to Friday 28 August 2026, 10:00am – 2:30pm, Grow Wilder, Bristol.

"Do you want to get into conservation, learn more about nature and wildlife or
meet like-minded people?"
events.summary: A three-day taster in practical conservation for 16 to 30 year olds at Grow Wilder, ending today — habitat work, wildlife identification and a route into the Trust's volunteering for people thinking about it as a career.
events.description:
A 3-day course offering young people behind-the-scenes experience at Avon
Wildlife Trust, covering wildlife conservation and land management. It provides
foundational knowledge in conservation work, practical fieldwork skills, and
insight into the various roles at the charity.

Day 1 focuses on land and habitat management, including practical conservation
tasks, discussions on sustainable practices, and horticultural work.

Day 2 covers ecology and wildlife monitoring through techniques like moth
trapping, mammal tracking, pond dipping, bird transects and owl pellet
dissection.

Day 3 addresses communication, education and advocacy within conservation, plus
wellbeing activities and career guidance.

For 16-30-year-olds. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL (what3words
frog.tested.tidy). Booking through the Eventbrite widget on the event page.

events.summary: August's translated fiction club takes Rene Karabash's She Who Remains, shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker and translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel.
events.description:
**Join us for an exciting evening to discuss translated literature. Whether you're a fan of literary fiction or just looking to try something new, this book club hopes to achieve just that. In August, we will be looking at Rene Karabash's She Who Remains, translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel, which was shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.**

***Date:***

Thursday 28th of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *SHE WHO REMAINS***

High in the Accursed Mountains, in a village ruled by the ancient laws of the Kanun, Bekija escapes an arranged marriage by becoming a sworn virgin, renouncing her womanhood to live as a man.

Her decision sets off a brutal chain of events, destroying her family and separating her from the one she loves the most.

Years later, as Bekija – now Matija – tells their story to a visiting journalist, long-buried truths come to light, along with the realisation of all that might have been.

***Shortlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.***

**ABOUT *PEIRENE PRESS***

Peirene Press is an award-winning independent publisher. Founded in 2008, specialising in bringing exciting literary fiction and novellas from around the world, especially Europe, to English-language readers.

https://www.peirenepress.com/

Discover the incredible filmmaking talent on your doorstep at the
Homegrown Cinema Showcase, a fun evening celebrating independent
films made right here in the South West.

answer your questions. It's a rare chance to experience original,

events.title: Forwards Festival 2026
events.timesText: Friday 14:00–23:00; Saturday and Sunday gates 12:00, close 23:00, last entry 20:00
events.raw:
**Bristol Forwards Festival 2026: All you need to know ahead of major Downs event** — Bristol Live, published 16 August 2026.

> This year, Forwards begins with 'Forwards Presents' on Friday, August 28, before the main festival gets underway on Saturday, August 29, and Sunday, August 30. All three days take place on the Downs, with Friday running from 2-11pm, and Saturday and Sunday's gates opening at 12pm and closing at 11pm, with last entry at 8pm. There is no re-entry to the festival.

Forwards Presents (Friday): Lorde headlines, with Djo making his Bristol debut, plus Audrey Hobert, Rose Gray, Esha Tewari, Grove, Maisie Peters and Girl Group.

Saturday: Tems, Self Esteem and Wet Leg top the bill, with Joy Crookes, Tricky, Goldie, Erika de Casier, Paraorchestra: Kraftwerk RE:WERK, Crazy P, RUBII, 1-800 GIRLS, The Itch, Xanadu, Mitch Sanders, TXN, August, Next Level Showcase and Maribou State.

Sunday: Little Simz, Amyl and The Sniffers and Dijon top the bill, with Viagra Boys, Oklou, Jim Legxacy, Princess Nokia, Jean Dawson, YHWH Nailgun, Wesley Joseph, Gena, anaiis, Ledbyher, Liim, Jamz Supernova, O'Flynn, Pack of Animals, Grandmas House and the Next Level Showcase.
events.summary: Bristol's big bank holiday festival on the Downs, over three days for the first time: Lorde and Djo on the new Friday, Tems, Self Esteem and Wet Leg on Saturday, Little Simz, Amyl and The Sniffers and Dijon on Sunday. No re-entry once you are in, and last entry is 20:00 on the Saturday and Sunday.

events.raw:
**Aardman Summer Special** — 28-31 August.

"Shaun the Sheep is coming to Bristol Zoo Project for Aardman's 50th Anniversary!"

"This August Bank Holiday ONLY, Shaun the Sheep will be joining us for a weekend of
fun at our Aardman Summer Special! Meet Shaun the Sheep, take part in Shaun's
Wildlife Mission trail, make your very own clay model of Shaun or get creative with

events.summary: Four days of Shaun the Sheep for Aardman's 50th: character meet-and-greets at regular intervals, a bookable clay-modelling Claystation in Bear Wood, a stamp-collecting Wildlife Mission trail and a free activity pack on entry. Free with zoo admission, and the last big thing on before term starts.
events.description:
Shaun the Sheep is coming to Bristol Zoo Project for Aardman's 50th Anniversary!

This August Bank Holiday ONLY, Shaun the Sheep will be joining us for a weekend of
fun at our Aardman Summer Special!

Meet Shaun the Sheep, take part in Shaun's Wildlife Mission trail, make your very
own clay model of Shaun or get creative with our fun activity pack! All FREE at
Bristol Zoo Project in celebration of Aardman's 50th Anniversary.

**Meet Shaun the Sheep!** Shaun will be at the zoo every day between 28-31 August
inclusive, making appearances at regular intervals throughout the day. So remember
to bring your camera when you visit!

**Join a Claystation.** Make your own Shaun the Sheep at our Aardman Claystation in
Bear Wood. Book your place online with your ticket.

**Complete your Wildlife Mission.** Join Shaun on a Wildlife Mission with Friends —
solve the challenges, collect the stamps and complete the mission!

**Activity packs.** Get your FREE activity pack on entry! Filled with baa-rilliant
crafts, puzzles and colouring.

All activities are FREE with entry!

More info: Aardman Claystations are free with a Bristol Zoo Project ticket or
membership; workshops must be booked online with your entry ticket. One booked slot
qualifies for one attendee. Carers must remain with children at all times during the
workshop. Head to Bear Wood Classroom for your timeslot. A self-led activity, guided
by an instruction sheet and a member of our team. You can take your model home with
you, a bag will be provided. Please note, animation is not part of the activity.
Recommended for ages 6+.

Shaun will be making regular appearances throughout the day; meeting him is free
with entry. Due to his popularity there will likely be a wait. Meet and greet takes
place at the picnic area opposite the Wilder gorilla sculpture and timings are
displayed on the area board. Activity packs can be collected at the entrance.

From the event terms: "There is no entry fee for the Claystation or Shaun the Sheep
Meet and Greet. However, it is only available to visitors to Bristol Zoo Project
between Friday 28 and Monday 31 August 2026."

events.description:
We've teamed up with Bristol legends Worm Disco Club to bring you
Summer Sessions — a three-month run of free Friday parties in our
sunny Old Market beer garden, powered by the Minirig Doppler
Soundsystem.

**Felix Joy** — One of Bristol's best, renowned for his morning show
on SWU.FM and his role in the seminal Sip the Juice DJ Collective,
Felix Joy will be bringing his usual eclectic mix of house, boogie,
break beats, and everything in-between.

**Kasia** — Kasia blends broken beat and soulful house with reggae,
rare groove and funk, weaving together deep rhythms and uplifting
energy.

**Nathan Worm** — Founder of Worm Disco Club and owner of Hot Wax
Records, Nathan's passion for collecting and sharing music runs deep.
Having played a pivotal role in some of the city's most iconic nights
out, he now curates a diverse vinyl selection at his record shop in
Bishopston. Nathan's ever-growing collection touches all corners of
the globe, resulting in expertly crafted DJ sets that span a vast
array of genres. Whether you're a seasoned crate-digger or just
looking for a great groove, there's something for everyone in his
selection.

Ticket Information: Free entry, fundraising tickets available thorugh
Headfirst, raising money for Caring in Bristol. 100% of the proceeds
of fundraising tickets will go to Wiper and True's charity partner for
2025, supporting their work in homelessness prevention in Bristol.

Photography Notice: Wiper and True may be taking photos and videos at
this event. If you prefer not to be included in any content, it is
your responsibility to speak to a member of the Wiper and True team at
the event to let them know.

folklore come to life through oral storytelling. Old stories are
given the space to become relevant and meaningful to contemporary

Reconnect with people through imagination. Reconnect with your

events.description:
The Scribes are a multi-award-winning hip hop three-piece whose unique blend of beatboxing, off the cuff freestyling and genre-spanning music has created a live show quite unlike any other on the scene today, with appeal ranging far beyond traditional hip hop fare.

They have consistently proven to be an impressive and engaging live act with 2019 festival appearances at Glastonbury, Wilderness Festival, Shambala, Boomtown Fair, Bearded Theory, Leopalloza, Maui Waui Festival, St Pauls Carnival, Tunes In The Dunes, Godney Gathering and many more and have toured extensively across the UK and onto Europe, including slots at prestigious venues such as Camden's Jazz Cafe, Cargo, Urban In Ibiza, Bristol's O2 Academy, Peterborough Arena and Italy's Metaponto Beach Festival.

The Scribes are also proud winners of both the Exposure Music Award's "Best UK Urban Act" and the EatMusic Radio Award's "Best Live Act", and have provided original music for BBC and Channel 4 television, as well as having their latest album, which features Akil The MC (Jurassic 5) and Too Many Ts, being featured regularly on both national and local radio and media including BBC 1Xtra and BBC Radio 1 Introducing.

The Scribes are hotly tipped as one to watch with live dates across the UK and Europe, as well as sharing the stage with the likes of Macklemore, Wu Tang Clan, Dizzee Rascal, Kelis, Rag N Bone Man, Example, Lethal Bizzle, The Wailers, Jurassic 5, Sugarhill Gang, KRS One, De La Soul, MF Doom, and Souls Of Mischief to name (drop) but a few.

events.title: Tower Tour
events.raw:
Step behind closed doors and climb the soaring tower of Bristol Cathedral on
a special guided tour that will take you through 900 years of history and
architecture.

Climb the 172 steps of Bristol Cathedral's Tower for a guided tour where
you'll learn how the Cathedral has evolved over time and the engineering
feats that have made it into the beautiful building you see today.

You will come face to face with some of the finest medieval bells in the
world, tales of Isambard Kingdom Brunel, and uncover the mysteries of the
original 12th-century abbey that once dominated College Green.

This tour involves ascending almost 200 steps up a spiral staircase which is
narrow in places, with low-hanging doorways and pipes along the route. To
make sure the tour is suitable for you and your group please consult the
terms and conditions below.

For Carers tickets please email visitorexperience@bristol-cathedral.co.uk

Sat 29 Aug | 11:00 - 12:15
events.summary:
The one tower climb in the bank holiday weekend's diary: 172 steps up the
spiral staircase past some of the finest medieval bells in the world, with
900 years of the building's history on the way. Saturday only — the
cathedral prints no Sunday or Monday tour.

events.title: Annie Gardiner - 'Sleeping Dogs' Album Launch
events.raw:
**Annie Gardiner - 'Sleeping Dogs' Album Launch** — Sat 29 August // 19:30.
Celebrate the album launch party for Annie Gardiner's second solo album 'Sleeping Dogs'. Special guests to be announced.
events.summary: Bristol songwriter and producer Annie Gardiner launches her second solo album on Crystal Fuzz Records, with support still to be announced.
events.description:
On this day Annie Gardiner celebrates the birth of second solo album 'Sleeping Dogs' on Crystal Fuzz Records. Released back in February, the follow up to 2021's 'Bloodletting' was met with critical acclaim.

Critically acclaimed artist, songwriter and producer Annie Gardiner celebrated the release of her second solo album, 'Sleeping Dogs', in 2025. Her music has been championed by BBC 6 Music, featured on the Freak Zone playlist, Adam Walton's BBC Radio Wales show, BBC Introducing and numerous other radio programmes nationally and internationally.

A Welsh-Scottish-Italian artist based in Bristol, Gardiner has built a diverse career spanning experimental songwriting, noise-rock, jazz-not-jazz, improvisation and electronic music. She gained a UK-wide underground following as the front person and bassist of noise-rock band Hysterical Injury, was one-third of Human Worth's post-rock outfit Olanza, and co-wrote and performed vocals on Run Logan Run's 2022 album 'Nature Will Take Care of You'. Singles from the album received airplay on BBC 6 Music, Jamie Cullum's BBC Radio 2 show and Verity Sharpe's 'Late Junction' on BBC Radio 3. In 2023, she joined Run Logan Run as a guest vocalist for their appearance on the BBC Introducing Stage at Glastonbury Festival.

A sought-after collaborator and improviser, Gardiner has performed on vocals, electronics and bass with various artists and ensembles. Alongside her artistic practice, Gardiner works as a music producer at Studio B in J&J Studios, Bristol, and is a Senior Lecturer in Songwriting at BIMM University.

**Tour of The Bristol Hippodrome**

Bristol Hippodrome theatre tours are held regularly each month where you can have a tour behind the scenes starting at 10am and lasting for approximately 2 hours.

Presented by one of The Bristol Hippodrome's knowledgeable guides, the tour will take you around front of house and backstage areas, and includes the history, the shows, the stars, and of course a smattering of gossip and ghost stories. An ideal way to spend a Saturday morning whether you've lived in Bristol all your life, are a regular theatre goer who wants to find out more or a visitor to our great city.

Tickets are just £26 including booking fees.

Tours do not include show ticket and are subject to availability.

Theatre Tours are not suitable for wheelchair users and those with mobility issues due to a number of staircases. If you have any access needs, please do get in touch before your visit via email: BristolCreativeLearning@atgentertainment.com.

events.title: Forwards Festival Bristol 2026
events.raw:
**Forwards Festival Bristol 2026** — 29 Aug 2026 - 30 Aug 2026. Location: Durdham Down - The Downs in Bristol.

"FORWARDS Festival returns to Bristol for another year with its most ambitious and..." TEMS, SELF ESTEEM, WET LEG, LITTLE SIMZ AND MORE!
events.summary: Forwards' fifth edition on Clifton Downs over the bank holiday weekend, headlined Saturday by Tems, Self Esteem and Wet Leg and Sunday by Little Simz, Amyl & The Sniffers and Dijon.
events.description:
**TEMS, SELF ESTEEM, WET LEG, LITTLE SIMZ AND MORE!**

FORWARDS Festival returns to Bristol for another year with its most ambitious and musically expansive programme to date. Taking place at Clifton Downs on Saturday 29th and Sunday 30th August 2026, the festival celebrates its fifth anniversary with a powerful lineup of global stars, genre-spanning artists, and boundary-pushing performances.

Across two days of music, culture and conversation, FORWARDS continues its mission to spotlight both internationally acclaimed acts and emerging voices — a formula that has helped it become one of the UK's most forward-thinking festivals.

### Headliners for the 2026 Lineup

Saturday's lineup is led by an all-female trio of headliners. Grammy Award-winning Nigerian superstar Tems will make her Bristol headline debut, bringing her soulful, globally influential take on R&B to the Downs. She will be joined by British pop powerhouse Self Esteem, known for her bold, theatrical performances and outspoken lyricism, and indie favourites Wet Leg, whose sharp wit and infectious energy have made them one of the UK's most exciting bands of recent years.

On Sunday, the festival shifts gears with another genre-spanning headline bill. Little Simz, the Mercury Prize-winning rapper widely regarded as one of the most important voices in British hip-hop, takes top billing alongside Australian punk firebrands Amyl & The Sniffers and acclaimed American singer-songwriter Dijon, who will also be performing in Bristol for the first time.

### Saturday 29th August

Tems · Self Esteem · Wet Leg · Joy Crookes · Tricky · Goldie (Live) · Paraorchestra presents Kraftwerk Re:Werk with Charles Hazlewood · Special Guests: Maribou State

### Sunday 30th August

Little Simz · Amyl & The Sniffers · Dijon · Viagra Boys · Oklou · Jim Legxacy · Princess Nokia · Jean Dawson · Gena ft. Liv.e & Karriem Riggins · Anaiis

### More Than a Music Festival

Since launching in 2022, FORWARDS has established itself as more than just a music event. Alongside the performances, the festival's "The Information" stage will return in 2026, offering discussions, debates and talks.

events.description:
FORWARDS: an inner city music festival drawing the biggest names in
international music to Bristol Downs. The festival aims to present high
quality, diverse and heritage music acts alongside emerging artists from
Bristol & beyond.

The festival presents a contemporary curation of music while paying homage
to Bristol's long standing history of being a music city. In addition,
FORWARDS is more than just a music festival, it looks to challenge what
metropolitan festivals can be today and how they can do good, from the
inside out. The 2-day festival aims to harness the power of live events to
bring people together for incredible music moments and lasting positive
change.

At the heart of the festival is FORWARDS THINKING, a platform for year round
social initiatives in Bristol, all through our partners, Big Team CIC and
Team Canteen CIC. Alongside these partners is The Information, a dedicated
space at FORWARDS for debate and understanding on today's current affairs
and cultural issues.

events.summary: Steam trips along the quayside on Bristol Harbour Railway behind the locomotive Henbury. The season opens on the bank holiday weekend and, unusually for a weekends-only service, runs the Monday too.
events.description:
Take a steam train ride on Bristol Harbour Railway from M Shed. The train will be pulled
by the locomotive Henbury.

Bristol Harbour Railway was built by the Great Western Railway in the 1870s and extended
in the 1900s. After a century as a goods railway, it was handed over to the museum and
has run as a heritage railway ever since. The railway runs on the quayside between
M Shed and the SS Great Britain.

Our two Bristol-built steam locomotives, Henbury and Portbury, served their working lives
on the docks railway system at Avonmouth. The wagons are types once commonly seen on the
docks at Avonmouth and here in the old City Docks.

**Upcoming dates for 2026**

- Saturday 29 to Monday 31 August
- Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September
- Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September
- Saturday 10 and Sunday 11 October
- Saturday 24 and Sunday 25 October
- Saturday 31 and Sunday 1 November

From 11am – subject to availability.

Please note, M Shed’s large working exhibits are operated by volunteers. Occasionally
crew shortages, mechanical difficulties or adverse weather conditions may force us to
alter or cancel the advertised event. We advise you to check with us to avoid
disappointment by calling 0117 352 6600.

**Booking information.** Please note train rides are running on weekends only. Buy
tickets on the day from the ticket office by the M Shed platform. Single £3.50 /
Return £5. Children under six years old travel free. Dogs welcome. From 11am – subject
to availability. Trips last approximately 15 minutes.

events.summary: Leeds punk-jazz six-piece Plantfood, a Headfirst editor's pick and the only thing The Canteen lists across the long weekend.
events.description:
*Headfirst Editor's Pick: "Free entry punk-jazz!? What's not to like? 'Specially when it's Plantfood's kitchen-sink pile-up of dub basslines, dizzying jungle jazz x afro-funk grooves and neverending dual sax transcendence. Leeds' brightest in a ones-to-watch taster session FFO: The Comet Is Coming, Black Country New Road, Melt Yourself Down."*

Plantfood are a blood-pumping jazz force summoning an onslaught of electronic and acoustic sounds with influences ranging from heavy hitters like The Prodigy to the spiritual explorations of John Coltrane. The 6-piece collective guides audiences through the extremes of the mosh pit to serene meditations. Forming within and coming up through the inspiring Leeds Jazz scene, Plantfood have quickly become a defining sound in the scene.

As featured on their debut album Carnivores, Yung Yusuf is an English-Palestinian rapper previously known as Yusuf Yellow. His lyrics are marked by a deep exploration of fear, identity, and vulnerability, while his playful wordplay and unique energy keep listeners on their toes.

Touring across the UK with sellout headline shows in London, Leeds, York, Falmouth, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge, Plantfood and Yung Yusuf have reached new sonic horizons, fusing Punk, Jazz and Electronica in bold and explosive arrangements. Alongside this, they have supported many established artists such as Dele Sosimi, BCUC and Nubiyan Twist.

"It's hard to keep still to that one, the bass and percussion alone produce enough energy to power the grid." — Soweto Kinch, BBC Radio 3

Free entry until 9.30pm, £6 after. + DJ Discobobulator Till Late.

Entry requirements: 18+

**What's My Age Again? Rock & Emo Deck Party** — Sat 29 Aug 26, club night at Thekla.

events.summary: Club night on the boat: What's My Age Again? Rock & Emo Deck Party.
events.description:
**What’s My Age Again? 25+ Rock & Emo Deck Party 🖤**

Calling all Elder Emos… We’re throwing it back for the kids who were Not Okay.

Join us aboard Thekla this August Bank Holiday for What’s My Age Again? – a 25+ day party packed with the Emo, Pop Punk and Nu-Metal anthems that soundtracked your youth.

We’re spinning all the classics from My Chemical Romance, Blink-182, Paramore, Linkin Park, Evanescence, Fall Out Boy, Limp Bizkit, Panic! At The Disco, You Me At Six, A Day To Remember, Avril Lavigne, the Offspring, Good Charlotte and so much more.

Expect…

🖤 All killer, no filler.

🎶 Only the biggest hits, with music played inside + outside.

🍸 Themed cocktails to enjoy in the sunshine.

☀️ Pure emo festival vibes.

🥀 25+

🛳️ Iconic venue with seating on top deck, smoking deck AND quayside.

✨ Themed decor throughout.

🎸 4-9pm. Party hard and home before your back hurts.

It’s not a phase and it never was.

Let’s scream like it’s 2005. 🖤

Tickets on sale now, with group bookings deals available. Don’t miss out.

**Thekla Dockside Sessions ☀️⚓**

_We’re very excited to bring you Dockside Sessions at Thekla**– your new go-to summer hotspot**. We’re taking over select Saturdays with a series of sun-soaked deck parties – taking place across the top deck, smoking deck AND the quayside. **🏖️**_

_That’s right, for this series only, we’re extending the party onto the quayside. You can get the full Thekla experience whether you’re chilling by the harbour, soaking up the sunshine or dancing on deck._

_Expect banging tunes, great drinks and immaculate summer vibes as we keep the hits flowing all afternoon long. Whether you’re partying by the DJ booth or chilling in the sun, we’ve got you covered on Bristol’s #1 floating venue._

**Here’s what’s in store…**

_✨ Six deck parties with something for everyone – ABBA to Emo, 80s Bangers to 90s Boybands, Dad Rock to Hip Hop + more

🕓 4-9pm on select Saturdays throughout summer

🎧 DJs spinning non-stop bangers, inside and out

🪑 Seating across the top deck, outdoor deck + the quayside

🍹 Cocktails & specially curated drinks menus

🎉 Themed decor throughout

👯 Group bookings deals & packages available_

_Grab your tickets, round up your crew and come party in the sunshine at your favourite harbourside hangout._

_See you on board. 🍹⚓_

events.description:
**PART CHIMP**

_Part Chimp have long made it their mission to shake speakers, fry brains and push volume to its limits. Underground legends of primal riffing, their fifth album Drool sees them sharpen that intensity into something even more focused and ferocious._

_Blending crushing heaviness with a skewed sense of melody, Drool channels echoes of Melvins and Sonic Youth while carving out a sound that’s wholly their own — pulverising, chaotic and strangely life-affirming. Tracks like Back From The Dead, Drool and Up, With Notes showcase a band revelling in the alchemy of loud amps, strange tunings and raw instinct._

_Recorded across London, New York and Somerset, the album captures the band at their most honest and unfiltered. Equal parts panic, chaos and catharsis, Part Chimp’s music thrives on the edge of collapse — shambolic, unpredictable and full of joy._

_Drool is loud, enveloping and uncompromising — a blast of heavy music that hits as hard as it exhilarates._

**AAA GRIPPER**

_AAA Gripper emerged from the first Wrong Speed Records festival in Glastonbury in 2023. Built from long bass-and-drum improvisations and shaped into tense, wiry post-punk, the band quickly developed a reputation for explosive live shows and unpredictable songwriting. Featuring members connected to acts including Sweet Williams and Hey Colossus, AAA Gripper balance tightly wound grooves with jagged guitar work and a restless experimental streak._

_Their debut album 'We Invented Work For The Common Good' dissects the absurdities of modern working life through frontman M. Edward Cole’s stream-of-consciousness lyrics, dark humour and anxious intensity. Channeling the rhythmic force of Fugazi and The Jesus Lizard, AAA Gripper have quickly become one of the UK underground’s most exciting new post-punk bands._

**RESURRECTION MEN**

_RESURRECTION MEN are a brand new heavy band, featuring members of SANS, Modern Rituals, and Talons._

**A-Sun Amissa x Lauren Mason/ Rowan Evans/ Samatar Elmi x Roscian** — Sun 30 Aug 2026, doors 14:15, Exchange.
