18+.
events.summary: A-Sun Amissa x Lauren Mason/ Rowan Evans/ Samatar Elmi x Roscian at Exchange, drone, experimental and poetry, doors 14:15.
events.description:
An afternoon featuring some of the UK's most innovative poets and musicians, collaborating across language and sound!

In _Water Scores,_ **Lauren Mason’s** dark and experimental poetics respond to **A-Sun Amissa’s** tide-like currents of guitar, synth, sampled hydrophone, loops, and clarinet. This long-form piece ranges through deep ambience, crashing chaos and ebbing aftermath. During this new work Mason explores the curses of corporate extraction and pollution on our planet’s water, and listens in, as water speaks back.

**Rowan Evans** will be performing his poem and sound sequence _The Last Verses of Beccán,_ plus some new material. Bilingual poetry and sound composition explore medieval hermitage, sea-exile, ecology and language hybridity, with field recordings made in the inner Hebrides. New unreleased material will combine Ancient Greek translation and dream lyric with tape samples, drum loops, synths and bass.

**Samatar Elmi and Roscian (solo)** will be performing a brand new collaboration featuring Samatar's highly charged political poetry, freestyle rap and gospel singing, alongside Roscian's darkly heavy synth and sample soundscapes. Not one to miss!

**Artist bios:**

**Lauren Mason** is best known as bassist with now-defunct existential sludge band Torpor, where she often wove her spoken word pieces through heavy soundscapes. She has been developing her poetic practice for many years and published her first pamphlet ‘Rust Canyon’ in 2025.

**A-Sun Amissa** are a group in a permanent state of metamorphosis, existing on the fringes of some kind of avant-rock, relentlessly pushing forward, shapeshifting and presenting their unique noise in new ways and on their own terms. A sound underpinned and overlaid with drones, moving in and around a diverse chasm of post-rock, melancholic drone, noise, doom and ambient sounds.

**Rowan Evans** is a poet, composer and sound artist whose debut collection _A Method, A Path_ (Bloomsbury Poetry, 2023) was shortlisted for the Forward Prize. His chapbook _The Last Verses of Beccán_ (Guillemot Press, 2019) won the Michael Marks Award for Poetry. He received an Eric Gregory Award in 2015 and a selection of his work appears in _Penguin Modern Poets 7: These Hard and Shining Things_ (Penguin, 2018). Evans records and performs music for theatre, dance, film and art installation.

**Samatar Elmi** is an award-winning writer, musician and educator. His debut pamphlet, ‘Portrait of Colossus’ (flipped eye press, 2021), was selected as a PBS Pamphlet Choice. His stunning debut collection, ‘The Epic of Cader Idris’ (Bloomsbury, 2024), includes the 2021 Geoffrey Dearmer Prize winning poem. His poems have appeared widely including in Poetry, Prairie Schooner, Poetry Review, Poetry Wales, Magma, and Iota and anthologised in More Fiya, Filigree, After Plath, and The Echoing Gallery. Elmi is an Obsidian Fellow, flipped eye press associate poetry editor, and is a specialist tutor in 'Neurodiversity and the Creative Process'. He is currently touring nationally throughout 2026, reading from a pair of collections ( Agen Bien Fou, Kulvert Books, 2026; and Reclamations: Disregard Prior Prompt ,Aout Fecit, 2026).

As Knomad Spock, his debut album, ‘Winter of Discontent’ was critically acclaimed in print (Clash Magazine, Afropunk, GoldFlakePaint, Equate Magazine) and radio (BBC 6 Music, BBC Wales, Amazing Radio, Radio X). His recent albums ‘A Darker Light’ and ‘Through the Walls’ are available on Bandcamp. He raps under his own name and has recorded with UK hiphop luminaries, Jesht and Chester P.

**Roscian (solo)** is Simon Mason, better known as drummer of existential sludge band Torpor. Roscian sees him creating a different kind of heaviness with synthesis and samples.

Doors 14:00 for a prompt start! Music over by 16:40

events.description:
An enchanting tale of ritual magic and misfortune set by the sea in 1917 – a brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre (*Barleycorn*, *The Cabinet of Madame Fanny Du Thé*)

Lizard Point, 1917. While the war grinds on in France, the mysterious Crow and his company of runaways spend their days in a fever of conjured dreams. In their refuge amongst the cliffs, hidden away from the prying eyes of the police, the troupe rejoice in strange rituals and tales of long-lost loves.

But the tides are turning. Crow has taken to watching the sea. The voices of the dead are getting louder. And when a soldier from the front line washes up on the rocks nearby, the truth about Crow, and Lizard Point, threatens to drown them all.

A brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre, conjuring a darkly comic blend of occult intrigue and enchanting live music.

**Performances:** Sun 30th August at 7:00 pm, Mon 31st August at 7:30 pm, Tue 1st September at 7:30 pm. Tickets £14. Running time 75 mins (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

**Skydaddy + Mia Wilson + Nile Robinson** — Mon 31 August // 19:00.
Virtuoso songwriting from far and near. FFO: Cameron Winter, Weyes Blood, BCNR, Rundgren, Nilsson.
events.summary: A bank holiday Monday triple bill of songwriters — London's Skydaddy midway through a run supporting Geese, Californian Mia Wilson making her UK debut, and Bristol-based Nile Robinson.
events.description:
the song has no ending present

Virtuoso songwriting from far and near FFO: Cameron Winter, Weyes Blood, BCNR, Rundgren, Nilsson

Skydaddy is the moniker of London-born Lebanese/Grenadian songwriter-producer/artist, Rachid Fakhre. He has released two mini-albums through his own label Bathtime Sounds as well as albums of his former project, Spang Sisters. This year he will be releasing his debut solo album and will be supporting Geese on their UK shows in the run-up. He (and his band) will be stopping off at The Cube for a very special show midway.

Southern California singer-songwriter Mia Wilson (and band) will be gracing the cube with her debut UK performance before going on to play End of the Road Festival. Mia's self titled LP - Produced by Tim Ramsey (Vetiver, Little Wings, Kacey Johansing) - blends piano and guitar based compositions with lush orchestral arrangements to create a backdrop for her introspective lyrics and captivating mezzo-soprano vocals. The album recalls the golden glow of late 60's & early 70's LA records like Carole King's Tapestry, Judee Sill's Heart Food, and Jackson Browne's Late For the Sky.

North Yorkshire born folk-songwriter Nile Robinson began performing live music after moving to Bristol in 2023. His work blends influences of American Primitive, Anti-Folk & Glock-Rock across an eclectic array of instrumentation.

events.description:
**Whether you’re a fan of the series or looking to delve into romance fiction, our Romance book club offers a joyful escape. We're building a community to gush over swoon-worthy characters and a safe space to discuss themes like relationships. With *ACOTAR 6* coming out this Autumn, our Romance Book Club is reading through the entire series in anticipation of its release. **

**In August, we will be looking at Books 3 and 4 in Sarah J Maas' *A Court of Thorns and Roses *Series. Let’s share the love!**

**Date:**
Monday 31st of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *A COURT OF WINGS AND RUIN (BOOK THREE)***

Feyre has returned to the Spring Court, determined to gather information on Tamlin's manoeuvrings and the invading king threatening to bring her land to its knees. But to do so she must play a deadly game of deceit – and one slip may spell doom not only for Feyre, but for her world as well.

As war bears down upon them all, Feyre must decide who to trust amongst the dazzling and lethal High Lords and hunt for allies in unexpected places. And her heart will face the ultimate test as she and her mate are forced to question whether they can truly trust each other.

**ABOUT *A COURT OF FROST AND STARLIGHT (BOOK FOUR)***

In this companion tale to the bestselling *A Court of Thorns and Roses** series*, Feyre, Rhys and their friends are working to rebuild the Night Court and the vastly changed world beyond after the events of *A Court of Wings and Ruin*.

But Winter Solstice is finally near, and with it a hard-earned reprieve. Yet even the festive atmosphere can't keep the shadows of the past from looming. As Feyre navigates her first Winter Solstice as High Lady, she finds that those dearest to her have more wounds than she anticipated – scars that will have a far-reaching impact on the future of their court.

***ABOUT SARAH J. MAAS***

**Sarah J. Maas** is the #1 bestselling author of the Court of Thorns and Roses, Throne of Glass, and Crescent City series. Her books have sold more than seventy-five million copies and are published in forty languages.

CRAMPS fans unite! Spectacular, psychotic tribute act NEW KIND OF CRAMPS are coming to 6 lucky cities in the UK this August!

A sensational and well-seasoned group of familiar-faced fiends summon the original, wild, sick, ghoulish masters of psychotic rock ‘n’ roll out of the grave and onto the stage.

This group of musicians have been seen by thousands of Cramps fans across the UK, racking up 4 tours between them, playing the legends’ back catalogue with such accuracy, even tribute sceptics who gave it a try loved them!

Bring in Kris Sinister to the mix and you know you’re ‘Concocting Chaos’ before they even start playing! The Italian rockabilly star (Rebel Garage/ The Dangerous Three) has been keeping the Cramps torch burning since the early 2000’s with his band “Kris and Lou”.

Immerse yourself in this zany show from Kris, Jess Furneaux, Kate ‘Drums’ Porter, Billy Miles Brooke & Harrison Wonderland who will take you on a wild ride and let’s face it, we all want a bit if fun and that’s all we’re here to do so let’s have a party!

Mutant Movement is a promoter with a resume packed full of Cramps shows, this tour will bring their total to 44 nights of mayhem, spreading the music of a band that will never be repeated.

Psycho/Rockabilly phenoms Galloping Dick will kick things off each night. Suave, yet Dangerous, Galloping Dick add a sinister glamour to their dark pyscho/rockabilly/garage repertoire, coupled with their notoriously killer live performances.

events.title: Searching for the Future - A decade of reportage illustration
events.raw:
**Searching for the Future - A decade of reportage illustration** —
Tue, 1 Sept 2026 10:00 – Tue, 8 Sept 2026 18:00.
Centrespace Gallery & Studios, 6 Leonard Lane, Bristol BS1 1EA.

For the duration of *Searching for the Future: A decade of reportage
illustration*, artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace
Gallery into a giant sketchbook. The illustrated stories of people
she's met will adorn the walls, resulting in a colourful display of
community.

**Exhibition Dates:** Tuesday 1st September - Tuesday 8th September
**PV:** Friday 4th September, 6:00 - 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 11:00 am - 6:00 pm
events.summary: Ten years of Niki Groom's reportage illustration, hung as if the gallery were one enormous sketchbook of the people she has drawn. The first show after the bank holiday gap.
events.description:
For this exhibition, artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace
Gallery into a giant sketchbook. The walls will carry the illustrated
stories of people she's met — life-size paintings of dancers and
musicians, and a celebration of events that bring people together, such
as festivals, protests, sport and food.

Groom has specialised in reportage illustration for the humanitarian
and cultural sectors since 2016, when she documented the Calais
'Jungle' for Choose Love — creating impactful imagery that allows
people to remain anonymous. She has worked with local organisations
including Refugee Women of Bristol and Bristol Refugee Festival.

The exhibition includes workshops, talks on creativity and community, a
sketching table, and merchandise featuring original artwork.

**Dates:** Tuesday 1 September 11:00 – Tuesday 8 September 2026 18:00
**Private View:** Friday 4th September, 6:00 – 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 11:00 am – 6:00 pm
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.title: Charity Shop World launch with Tansy E. Hoskins

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**Charity Shop World launch with Tansy E. Hoskins** — Bookhaus

Tuesday 1st September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "The feel-good alternative to the skip and the
shopping centre, or just another stop on the conveyor belt? Tansy E.
Hoskins' Charity Shop World delivers a reality check on the afterlife of
your donated wares, interweaving far-reaching research into overconsumption
with her personal experiences of the shop floor."
events.summary: Tansy E. Hoskins on what actually happens to the bags you drop at the charity shop, from the sorting floor to overseas landfill. Ticket includes a drink and £2 off the book.
events.description:
Have you ever wondered what happens to the contents of the bags you drop off
at the charity shop?

With over 80 billion pieces of clothing produced each year and with human
made stuff now outweighing living biomass, this is the story of the first
sorting site for the deluge of items we discard every single day.

Having spent decades exploring charity shops for bargains and treasure,
Tansy Hoskins decided to dig deep into the world of charity shop
volunteering. From used underwear to wolf pelts, *Charity Shop World* is a
personal account of sorting through donations to reveal the entanglement of
people and products. This book also investigates the export of clothes to
overseas markets and landfill, revealing hidden shareholders behind a
multi-million pound business.

Taking us to the heart of a country hit by austerity and the cost of living
crisis, *Charity Shop World* reveals surprising places of human
connectivity, where local communities struggle to find their way through
economic hardship to reach a more sustainable way of living.

Tansy will be joining us to discuss all this. Tickets cost £7 and include a
glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.title: The World Beneath Our Feet launch with Frank Ashwood

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £3 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**The World Beneath Our Feet launch with Frank Ashwood** — Bookhaus

Wednesday 2nd September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "Subterranean ecologist Frank Ashwood launches a
low-key revolution in pop-science soil biodiversity. He's in the Haus
lifting the lid on the neglected universe of beetles, earthworms, microbes
and life-giving dirt."
events.summary: Soil ecologist Frank Ashwood on the most biodiverse habitat on the planet, in conversation with Josiah Judson of the Soil Association. Drink and £3 off the book included.
events.description:
To appreciate the wonders of the world around us, we're often told to look
up. But what if we need to look down instead?

Everything that happens below ground sustains all life above it — yet we
rarely think about this mysterious, dark underland. In *The World Beneath
Our Feet* soil ecologist Frank Ashwood scratches the surface and takes us on
an eye-opening safari through this precious ecosystem, from the ancient
forests of New Zealand to the vast black soil deposits of the US and China.

The ground beneath our feet hums with a staggering abundance of winding
roots, interconnecting fungal networks, wriggling creatures and mind-blowing
microbial life. This hidden ecosystem is the single most biodiverse habitat
on the planet. Half of all our species exist underfoot, and just a handful
of soil can contain an entire world. Without soil, there would be no life as
we know it.

In a story of connection and communication, we meet pioneering plants and
minute animals that are essential to the health and wellbeing of our planet.
We learn how soil makes our very existence possible, allowing us to
cultivate crops as well as storing precious carbon and the water we need to
survive.

Frank Ashwood will be in conversation with Josiah Judson (Soil Association).
Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £3 off the
book. Presented by bookhaus.

Josiah is a soil scientist within the Soil Association's Farming and Land
Use team, contributing to European research programmes and advising on
technical soil health issues in the UK.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.raw: **The Light House** — Weds 2nd Sept 2026. 7.30pm. £14. Alys Williams & Company present a real-life love story about holding onto each other, even in the darkest times – tender, funny and defiantly hopeful, it's a love letter to life
events.summary: Alys Williams & Company's true-story love letter to holding on, one night only.
events.description:
*'Man overboard, man overboard! Call control. Blow the whistle.'*

Love is a complicated business. It gets even more complicated when the person you love doesn't want to be alive. Tender, funny and defiantly hopeful, *The Light House* is a real-life story of falling in love and staying in love, even when the lights go out and you're lost in the dark. Join the emergency response as we dance in the kitchen, sing in the streets and try to turn the lights back on. It gets lonely, muddling through these days and nights. So why don't we do it together?

*The Light House* is the highly acclaimed debut play of theatre artist, Aly Williams.

**Date:** Wednesday, 2nd September 2026, 7:30pm. Tickets £14. Running time 1 hour (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

**Content warnings:** References to depression, suicide/suicidal ideation and hospitalisation.

Conscious Living programme entails.
events.summary: A free online orientation for UWE's eight-week Mindful Eating course, including a short guided practice. Open to anyone over 18.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how they relate to our moods
and emotions. In time, we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** The orientation session is a chance to find
out more about the course and ask any questions you may have. It will
also be an opportunity for you to experience a short practice in a small
group environment, which can help you to assess whether this course is
right for you at this time. Upon completion of your orientation session,
you will be invited to formally register on the course and pay your
course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System. Attendance at the orientation
session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

events.description:
A night of political, social and cultural comedy featuring some of the
most exciting grassroots comedians of Bristol and beyond – and the acts
ACTUALLY get paid. Come join the revolution!

The founding principle is platforming comedians with a message (think
counter-culture, underrepresented, original) and ensuring that they're
paid for their craft. There are no headliners, so each performer's
comedic voice gets room. Proceeds support the collectively owned PRSC
building: the more they make through tickets, the more they can pay
acts, so attendees are encouraged to contribute what they can afford.

The night has won multiple Chortle awards, including Best Comedy Format
2026 for South West & Wales.

16+; under 18s must be accompanied by a 21+ adult on a 1:1 ratio. Bar

events.title: Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night
events.raw: **Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night** — Sep 5, 19:30–23:00. £5.
events.summary: A fusion social dance party — partner dancing without the baggage — opening with an all-levels intro workshop and running into DJ sets. No partner or experience needed; sliding-scale entry.
events.description:
We throw dance parties where all bodies are invited. You already know
how to dance, we're just here to give you permission to embrace all of
the ways your body wants to move.

The evening opens with an all-levels workshop at 7:45pm, with local
teachers offering an intro to social dancing, followed by DJs playing
tracks ranging from slow and squishy to high-energy bangers. No partner
or prior experience is necessary.

One core principle: be excellent to one another — respect boundaries
and consent. Fusion is partner dancing, without the baggage, fusing
various dance styles through improvisation. The organisers note their
approach is queer, it is feminist, and they don't want anyone left
behind.

The single-level venue provides accessible entry from pavement to
dancefloor, with modifications available on request.

Sliding scale: £5 (low income), £10 (general release), £15
(pay-it-forward). Tickets via hdfst.uk/kaleidoscope-fusion.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Andrew Bird Featuring Javier Jarquin & compere Ross Smith

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly show from The Comedy Box featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ANDREW BIRD

Andrew Bird is a top headline act throughout the UK and Ireland and has performed all around the world. He is highly in demand as a tour support for big name comics such as Rhod Gilbert, Rob Brydon, Jon Richardson and Michael McIntyre playing venues such as Wembley and O2 arenas, and is one of the hardest working TV warm-up acts in the industry having worked on shows as varied as Pointless, Have I Got News For You, The Jonathan Ross Show and Taskmaster.

There is a very good reason for Andrew Bird’s popularity. He is always funny and frequently hilarious. He’s a nimble storyteller, with a relaxed, personable style. He simply proves cracking company, whether he’s got an angle or not. Fast, fluid and animated, you might mistake his relentless chatter for a spontaneous stream of consciousness, were it not so effortlessly reliable in generating laughs.

#### “*A great storyteller, funny, likeable and effortless*” Time Out

#### “*Comedy gold…Bird’s going to be a big star, catch him close-up now*” The Scotsman

#### [andrewbirdcomedian.com](https://www.andrewbirdcomedian.com/)

events.raw:
**Free mindful eating information session** — Mon 07 September 2026, 10:30
- 12:00, online: Microsoft Teams. Free, booking required. A free session
explaining mindfulness and mindful eating, and what the Mindful Eating -
Conscious Living programme entails.
events.summary: The second, morning orientation session for UWE's Mindful Eating course, online and free to attend.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how it relates to our moods
and emotions. In time we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** If you are interested in this course, you
will be invited to attend an orientation session. The orientation session
is a chance to find out more about the course and ask any questions you
may have. It will also be an opportunity for you to experience a short
practice in a small group environment, which can help you to assess
whether this course is right for you at this time. On completion of your
orientation session, you will be invited to formally register on the
course and pay your course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System.
Attendance at the orientation session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

events.summary: A free evening with Professor Rory Cormac on the Information Research Department, Britain's secret Cold War disinformation unit, followed by a Q&A chaired by the Bristol Radical History Group's Rosie Wild. Book ahead.
events.description:
Bristol Radical History Group and Bookhaus are delighted to present Professor
Rory Cormac speaking about his new book *Fakers*, a history of Britain's
little known governmental disinformation and propaganda unit, the
Information Research Department.

Published in May 2026, *Fakers: a top-secret tale of phantoms and forgeries
on the disinformation front line* is based on 8,000 recently declassified
documents and covers the Information Research Department's covert work
countering communism from the 1950s to its demise in 1977. It offers
important insight into current questions of countering disinformation and in
conceptualising Black Propaganda more widely.

Professor Cormac's international archival research provides insight into how
the IRD's targets and recipients perceived British propaganda and the
process by which propaganda was developed, highlighting the role of local
and regional actors in places like Sub-Saharan Africa.

The event is free, but please book your place in advance. Professor Cormac's
talk will be followed by a Q&A with the audience, chaired by BRHG's Rosie
Wild, who has researched the IRD's domestic connections with Britain's secret
SDS spycops unit.

Rory Cormac is a Professor of International Relations at the University of
Nottingham and a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society. He is the author or
co-author of six books, including *How to Stage a Coup* (2022), *Disrupt and
Deny* (2018), and *The Secret Royals* (2021).

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.title: The Breaking of the English Working Class launch with Jonas Patrick Marvin

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**The Breaking of the English Working Class launch with Jonas Patrick
Marvin** — Bookhaus

Tuesday 8th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "Jonas Patrick Marvin safely detonates his tome of
socialist history in Bookhaus; The Breaking of The English Working Class is
a radical revision of our impossibly fractured class consciousness at a time
when we might need it the most."
events.summary: Jonas Patrick Marvin on forty years of class politics from Thatcher to the gig economy, with Shanice McBean, his co-host on The Life of the Party podcast.
events.description:
What has become of the English working class in the twenty-first century?

After a decades-long absence, class is once again central to our
understanding of ailing Britain. But what does it mean to be working class
today? As Jonas Patrick Marvin shows, questions of class have often been
replaced by talk of race and geography. Meanwhile, a collective identity
capable of pushing for change has become increasingly weakened and sidelined.

Retelling the story of the working class over the last forty years — from
Thatcher's war against the unions to New Labour neoliberalism — Marvin shows
how power and capital have combined to shatter a radical identity into many
parts: white, male, northerner, homeowner, immigrant, unemployed, disabled.
These fragments are then set in conflict against each other. Blending
political analysis with an account of his own experiences of class in London
and the rustbelt Midlands, Marvin shows how the working class have been
demonised and managed into impotence.

The working class is more than just an identity. As Marvin argues, it
embodies a collective will to demand change, one that can — and must — be
rekindled.

Jonas will be here at bookhaus to discuss all this in conversation with
Shanice McBean, his co-presenter on The Life of the Party podcast. Tickets
cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the book.
Presented by bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

Tuesday 8th September, Gloucester Road Bookshop at 7.00 pm

events.summary: The shop opens its autumn season with Karishma Jobanputra's debut short story collection, in conversation with the poet and novelist Nell Osborne.
events.description:
Our autumn events programme begins with the brilliant Karishma Jobanputra
who will be discussing her scintillating short story collection, *The Body
of the Thing*, in conversation with award-winning poet and novelist, Nell
Osborne.

One of 2026's most anticipated debuts, the stories in *The Body of the
Thing*, at their core, examine the myriad ways in which women negotiate all
manner of body politics. Written with great wit and a fierce sensitivity,
it's a stunner of a first outing, making this an event not to be missed!

Here's more on the book from its award-winning publisher, And Other Stories:

> A lyrical and visceral short story collection, *The Body of the Thing*
> unpicks the hierarchies that thrum under our relationships. Moving from
> bougie neighbourhoods in Manhattan to the sun-drenched piazzas of Italy,
> from coastal Maine to the bustle of London, these stories chase the
> fallout when women's bodies are valued for their beauty and youth,
> dismissed and discarded when ill, or made useful as parents and
> caregivers. Fluid, sensual, and fearless, *The Body of the Thing* explores
> motherhood, body dysmorphia and eating disorders, and celebrates female
> desire in all its complicated wonder.

Karishma Jobanputra is a British-Indian writer currently based in London. A
graduate of Columbia University's MFA Fiction Programme, her work has been
listed for the Brick Lane Short Story Prize and The Disquiet Literary Prize.
*The Body of the Thing* is her debut publication.

Nell Osborne is a poet and novelist. Her debut novel, *Ghost Driver* (Moist
Books, 2025), jointly won the Queen Mary Small Press Fiction Prize in 2026.

# Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 – The Toolbox

This introductory woodworking course teaches students to create a
softwood toolbox with a handle and inset base using traditional hand
tools and corner rebate joints. Upon completion, participants take
home their finished toolbox and gain foundational skills to pursue
home projects or advance to Level 2 classes.

**LEARN HOW TO:**

- Sawing straight and square
- Accurately marking out and cutting joints
- Effectively using hand tools including chisels and planes
- Fitting and finishing woodwork projects

**Skill level:** "Suitable for those with no previous woodwork
experience or, more experienced woodworkers wanting to improve their
skills and accuracy."

**Course options available:**

1. Thursday or Friday Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 3:40pm
2. Tuesday Evening Classes — 6:20pm to 8:45pm
3. Weekend Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 4:40pm

Birdwatchers have performed extensively in Bristol and won the Improv Cagematch in 2019.

—

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**Up the Youth Club with Emma Warren** — Bookhaus

Wednesday 9th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.
events.summary: Emma Warren on a century of British youth clubs — from Victorian boys' and girls' clubs to the rooms that produced The Specials and Stormzy — and what their disappearance costs.
events.description:
'Youth clubs have always existed. They always will, because there will
always be young people. How we care for our youth, and what we owe them, is
a question for all of us.'

In *Up the Youth Club*, Emma Warren maps the shifting story of youth clubs in
the UK and Northern Ireland, from factory workers in Victorian Boys' and
Girls' clubs to renegade self-emancipatory spaces in the 1970s and the
music-generating youth clubs of more recent decades. With a mixed lineage in
church evangelism, the patronage of the upper classes, grassroots' DIY, and
erratic state funding, the youth club has had a huge, yet almost invisible,
effect on music, sport, culture and society.

Arguing that we cannot advocate for what we do not understand, Warren
positions youth clubs as a kind of engine room — from the famous success
stories to come out of their doors, such as The Specials or Stormzy, to the
untold stories of young people finding shelter, sustenance and stimulation
for over a century — and why their dwindling numbers, largely due to
austerity and funding cuts, is of serious concern for us all.

With this impassioned history, Warren invites us to pick up the torch and
play an active part in protecting and re-igniting this vital part of UK
society.

Emma will be in conversation about this here at bookhaus. Tickets cost £7
and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by
bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.description:
**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In September, we'll be delving into *The Correspondent *by Virginia Evans, winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 9th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *The Correspondent***

***Winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction***

Every morning, Sybil Van Antwerp sits down to write letters – to her brother, to her best friend, to the president of the university who will not allow her to attend a class she desperately wants to take, to her favourite authors to tell them what she thinks of their latest books, and to one person to whom she writes often yet never sends the letter. Because at seventy-three, Sybil has used her correspondence – witty and wise – to make sense of the world.

But beyond the page, she has spent the last thirty years keeping the people who love her at arms’ length... Until letters from someone in her past force her to examine one of the most painful periods of her life. Now, Sybil must send the letter she has been writing for all these years - and find forgiveness within herself in order to move on.

Sybil Van Antwerp’s life of letters might not be an extraordinary one, but she also might be one of the most memorable characters you will ever read.

events.summary: A six-week beginners' course covering breathwork, meditation, movement and yoga philosophy, deliberately run in blocks with gaps between so the practice has time to settle.
events.description:
Get ready to build your yoga foundation in this 6-week course that
will leave you feeling centered and strong.

Yoga Foundations — 6-Week Beginners Course (formerly Yoga for
Beginners at Yogasara)

- St Anne's House, BS4
- Wednesdays, 6.00–7.00pm
- 9 September – 14 October

**What this course is about**

This 6-week course offers a gentle, supportive introduction to yoga.
We'll explore the four core elements of practice:

- Breathwork, to calm and steady the nervous system
- Meditation, simple practices for presence and perspective
- Asana (movement), building strength, steadiness and mobility
- Yoga philosophy, practical ideas you can take into everyday life

You don't need any experience, and you don't need to be flexible.
This isn't about achieving shapes, it's about learning how to work
with your body, your breath and your attention in a way that actually
supports real life.

**How the course is structured, and why**

This course runs several times a year, by design.

We learn together over six weeks, then there is space between courses
to integrate. Time to practise at home, attend regular classes with
new understanding, and notice what changes when you live with the
practices rather than rushing on to the next thing.

This is how learning really sticks.

When we repeat a practice, pause, and then return to it, the brain
lays down stronger neural pathways. Things that felt abstract start
to make sense in the body. You hear familiar instructions
differently. You move and breathe from a more informed, embodied
place.

Each time you return, you're not starting again, you're building on
lived experience.

**Saturday morning workshops, between courses**

In the spaces between the 6-week courses, I also offer Saturday
morning workshops for those who'd like to go a little deeper.

Bristol's legendary, bold, endlessly inventive and genre-defying theatre company, Action Hero (*The Talent*, *Oh Europa*, *Watch Me Fall*) return with something brand new: Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage after 8 years to conquer his stage fright and banish his ghosts, but he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it.

Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage. In an attempt to conquer an 8-year period of intense stage fright – and inside a dream-world inhabited by the phantoms of his disapproving ancestors – he is replaying his own autobiography and starting to lose the plot. But he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it. Instead, he's determined to keep the show on the road, re-writing his anxiety dreams live on stage in the hope of banishing the ghosts of performances past.

*A Song & Dance* is an absurdist nightmare of a performance about masking, performing and 'acting the part'.

events.description:
A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and celebrate 100 years
of public ownership.

Each walk focuses on an aspect of the estate’s rich wildlife, its historical connections or
its archaeological discoveries. Walk leaders will take you for a gentle stroll to different
parts of the park sharing what makes the Blaise Estate so special.

**Walk programme**

- **Hidden Blaise** — Join the estate rangers for a guided tour around the estate and visit
  areas usually closed to the public. Sunday 25 October, 11am–12:30pm.
- **Blaise Community Garden** — A guided tour around the Community Garden to learn about
  the history of the site and how its changed over the years. Saturday 19 September,
  2pm–3pm.
- **Archaeology and wildlife** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and the Bristol Regional
  Environmental Records Centre (BRERC) to find out more about Blaise’s archaeological
  discoveries and rich wildlife. Thursday 10 September, 11am–12:30pm.
- **Humphrey Repton’s landscape** — Explore the picturesque parkland created for the
  Harford Family by the famous landscape designer Humphrey Repton. Thursday 8 October,
  11am–12:30pm.
- **St Mary’s Church and churchyard** — A guided walk exploring St Mary’s church and
  churchyard, the historic memorials and its links to Bristol’s merchant history. Thursday
  22 October, 11am–12:30pm.

**Book tickets.** Free, donations welcome. Booking essential. Please select the walk or
walks you are interested in and book your place.

All walks last around 90 minutes and start from Blaise Museum unless otherwise stated.
Please arrive at least five minutes before the start of the walk. Suitable outdoor clothing
and a bottle of water are recommended. This event may have to be cancelled at short notice
due to external factors such as weather conditions. Well behaved dogs on leads are only
permitted on walks that specify this.

events.title: Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism

price.text: £30 includes a copy of the book / £6 general admission

events.raw:
**Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism**

Friday 11th September 2026, 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

A major analysis as we head into a dangerous new world order where China
and Russia threaten major change to the world's democracies
events.summary: The former Newsnight economics editor on *Reds*, his global history of communism from antiquity to the digital present, in conversation with Andrew Kelly.
events.description:
It starts in antiquity, not in 1917. It centres not just on the obvious
leaders and thinkers but asks how the idealism of millions of working-class
activists could lead to their acquiescence in mass murder, repression and
social atomisation. A fact whose legacy — unfortunately — is alive and
kicking in both Russia and China today.

Paul Mason's startling new book will argue that the desire to live without
hierarchy and property is an impulse deeply rooted in our human nature.
*Reds* traces the history of communist ideas through revolts in the ancient
and medieval worlds, and chronicles the rise of 19th century anti-capitalist
movements. Using first hand testimonies of both the perpetrators and the
victims, Mason gives a new and terrifying account of how the 20th century
experiment in communism turned into a totalitarian nightmare.

But, he argues, the story is not over. Western democracies are stagnant and
lacking self-belief. Looming climate chaos demands radical economic answers.
Millions of people in the global south see China's offer of authoritarian,
state-led development model as a viable alternative. And among the Western
left, new forms of techno-egalitarianism vie with right-wing libertarianism
in the battle over the digital future.

Paul Mason is a British journalist, author, broadcaster, and political
commentator known for his economic and political analysis. Formerly
Economics Editor at BBC Newsnight and Channel 4 News, he has written for
The New European, Social Europe, and Frankfurter Rundschau, authored books
like *Postcapitalism* and *How to Stop Fascism*, produced award-winning
documentaries, and is active in progressive politics and defence policy.

He will be in conversation with Andrew Kelly.

events.summary: Bordeaux's opera house opens its season with an all-Bernstein programme, beamed live to the Big Screen on Millennium Square. Free, bring a picnic.
events.description:
Join us for a free, live outdoor screening of the Opéra National de Bordeaux's opening
concert of their 2026-2027 season.

'Concert dans la Ville: Bernstein Story' will be broadcast live from the Auditorium of
Bordeaux to the Big Screen on Millennium Square.

Pack a picnic and be transported to the rhythms of Broadway by one of France's most
prestigious orchestras, Orchestre National Bordeaux Aquitaine.

This concert will be broadcast at venues across the Bordeaux region. We're delighted to
be able to share in celebrating music together as part of Bristol and Bordeaux's twinning
partnership.

**Programme — Leonard Bernstein.** *Fancy Free*, Three Dance Variations; *On the
Waterfront*, Suite Symphonique; *On the Town*, Three Dance Episodes; *West Side Story*,
Danses Symphoniques; *Candide*, Ouverture. Musical Director: Joseph Swensen.

Deckchair seating will be available on a first come, first served basis, so feel free to
bring your own camping chairs or beanbags too.

The Bristol Bordeaux Partnership celebrates it's 80th anniversary next year, with an
itinerary of events planned across the city to mark eight decades of friendship and
cultural exchange.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Steve Bugeja Featuring Eleanor Tiernan plus compere Meryl O’Rourke

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly show from The Comedy Box featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: STEVE BUGEJA

Steve Bugeja is one of the circuit’s most exciting comedians. Steve hosted the BBC Radio 4 series Economics with Subtitles and has made numerous appearances on TV shows including The Russell Howard Hour (Sky One), Love Island: Aftersun (ITV2), Russell Howard’s Stand Up Central (Comedy Central) and Zoe Ball on Saturday (ITV1).

Making a name for himself internationally, Steve has twice been invited to perform at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, appearing on Opening Night Comedy Allstars Supershow (ABC1) and on Comedy Up Late (ABC1).

A prolific writer, Steve was a key member of the writing team for The Russell Howard Hour (Sky One) and for Iain Stirling’s CelebAbility (ITV2) and has contributed material to Mock the Week (BBC2), 8 Out of 10 Cats (Channel 4) and BBC Radio 4.

Steve won the BBC New Comedy Award in 2013 and has since performed numerous Edinburgh Fringe shows and national tours.

#### “*Plentiful jokes and compelling storytelling*” — The Scotsman

#### “*Drum-tight, as if polished by a sitcom writers’ room to cram as many jokes in as humanly possible*” — Chortle

#### “*Blends the intelligence of a well-crafted hour with some touching emotional honesty*” — The Scotsman

[STEVE BUGEJA](https://www.stevebugeja.com/)

events.title: Youth Event: Evening Bat Walk in Stoke Park
events.raw:
**Youth Event: Evening Bat Walk in Stoke Park** — Saturday 12 September 2026,
6:00pm – 8:00pm, Grow Wilder, Bristol.

"Join us for an evening walk through Grow Wilder and across to Stoke Park to see
some great bats in action!"
events.summary: A dusk walk out of Grow Wilder and over into Stoke Park with detectors, listening for the bats working the hedgerows. Part of the Trust's youth programme, meeting at the growing site.
events.description:
Did you know there are 18 different species of bat in the UK? Did you know they
are the only true flying mammals in the world? Join us for an evening walk
through Grow Wilder and across to Stoke Park to see these great creatures in
action.

The event involves discussion of bat habitats, yearly cycles and conservation
needs, along with use of bat detectors to identify the species observed during
the walk. No prior expertise is required.

Participants should prepare for outdoor conditions with sturdy shoes,
appropriate clothing and a torch, as the return journey will occur in darkness
over uneven terrain.

This event is part of our Youth Programme so we ask anyone attending to be
between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome. Meet at Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park
Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL.

events.title: John Boorman and Bristol: Part II
events.ageRestriction: 16+, any under 18s accompanied by 21+ adult 1:1 ratio
events.raw:
**John Boorman and Bristol: Part II** — 12th Sep 12pm, runtime 4hrs 30mins.

Before he went on to Hollywood fame, film director John Boorman worked at BBC Bristol
where he made many films about the city. Five documentaries and one fictional film,
almost all set in Bristol and the West of England. None of these titles have been seen
for decades. With thanks to the BFI National Archive and the BBC Archive.
events.summary: Six BBC Bristol films John Boorman made before Hollywood — Concorde at Filton, art students, Citizen 63 portraits — unseen for decades, on the city's biggest screen.

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off each book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**In Conversation with Stacey Yu and Freya Bromley** — Bookhaus

Monday 14th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.
events.summary: A double bill of debut novelists: Freya Bromley on sisters and complicated families in *A Real Piece of Work*, Stacey Yu on falling in love with your boyfriend's cat in *Kitten*.
events.description:
We are very pleased to be joined by two rising literary stars for a double
header, in which Freya Bromley and Stacey Yu will be in conversation.

Freya will be here to discuss *A Real Piece of Work*. What does it mean for
a stranger to think you're brave? *A Real Piece of Work* is a sparkling and
spiky story of complicated families and even more complicated sisters,
narrated with tenderness, nuance and wit.

Stacey will be discussing *Kitten*. A magnetic novel about a young woman who
falls in love with her boyfriend's cat. Delicately playful and unexpectedly
heartfelt, *Kitten* is a sensitive reckoning with the allure of helplessness
and the uncertainty of becoming yourself in a world that is as disorienting
as it is full of hope and connection.

Join Freya and Stacey as they discuss their novels here at bookhaus. Tickets
cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off each book.
Presented by bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.summary: The crime club takes Raymond Chandler's The Big Sleep — classic noir, Philip Marlowe, no prior reading required.
events.description:
**Whodunnit? Let's find out together! Our Crime and Thriller Book Club is built for readers who love the thrill of a good chase. Whether you're a lifelong fan of golden-age whodunnits or looking to dive into the genre for the first time, our goal is to create a welcoming, lively space to share theories, analyse motives, and celebrate great storytelling. Each month, we'll gather in person to dissect everything from the atmospheric pacing of classic thrillers to the complex puzzles of modern murder mysteries. **

**In September, we will be discussing *The Big Sleep *by Raymond Chandler: a classic noir that follows a cynical private investigator, Philip Marlowe.**

**Date:**
Monday 14th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *THE BIG SLEEP***

Los Angeles PI Philip Marlowe is working for the Sternwood family.

Old man Sternwood, crippled and wheelchair-bound, is being given the squeeze by a blackmailer, and he wants Marlowe to make the problem go away. But with Sternwood's two wild, devil-may-care daughters prowling LA's seedy backstreets, Marlowe's got his work cut out, and that's before he stumbles over the first corpse...

*The Big Sleep* is Raymond Chandler's first novel featuring laconic PI Philip Marlowe.

***ABOUT RAYMOND CHANDLER***

Raymond Thornton Chandler was born in Chicago in 1888, but moved to England with his family when he was twelve, where he attended Dulwich College, alma mater to some of the twentieth century's most renowned writers. Returning to America in 1912, he settled in California, worked in a number of jobs, and later married.

It was during the Depression era that he seriously turned his hand to writing, and his first published story appeared in the pulp magazine *Black Mask* in 1933, followed six years later, when he was fifty, by his first novel, *The Big Sleep.*

Chandler died in 1959, having established himself as the finest crime writer in America.

events.raw:
**Tice Cin: Safe Spaces**

Monday 14th September 2026, 6:30 pm

Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD

Price range: £8.00 through £15.00
events.summary: The author of *Keeping the House* returns with her second novel, *Safe Spaces*, in conversation with Ralf Webb. Tickets can be bought with a discounted pre-order of the book.
events.description:
We are stoked to welcome a truly singular literary talent to Bristol in
September: Tice Cin will be with us to discuss her second novel *Safe
Spaces*!

As longtime fans of Cin's debut novel *Keeping The House*, we are especially
excited to be hosting — expect an enlivening and perspective-altering chat
about a book which is already gathering incredible praise. Tice will be in
conversation with Ralf Webb.

Pre-order your copy of *Safe Spaces* (rrp £14.99) for a special discounted
price with your ticket, then collect on the night!

**About Tice Cin.** Tice Cin is an interdisciplinary artist and author from
North London. Her debut novel *Keeping the House* (2021) received a Somerset
Maugham Award and a London Writers Award, was a Guardian Book of the Year
and was shortlisted for a British Book Award and the Desmond Elliot Prize.
Her BBC Radio 4 documentary *How Much Can You Say?* (2024) won an Audio
Production Award. She is the founder of the interdisciplinary production
company Neoprene Genie. Cin's sophomore novel *Safe Spaces* will be
published by Granta in September 2026.

**About Safe Spaces.** Our unnamed narrator survives in London and Newark on
a combination of Universal Credit, music production and songwriting, trying
to figure out what she wants from home, and whether anyone is prepared to
give it to her. Navigating love affairs and halted by pain following the
loss of her closest confidante, *Safe Spaces* is a portrait of the artist as
a young musician. At once a songbook, a found poem of place, a therapy
transcript and a community journal, it is a work of extraordinary lyricism
and candour.

events.raw:
**The Folk House Choir** — Day: Tuesday. Time: 19:00 to 21:00. Course code: D. Tutor: Nonny Tabbush.

Full fee: £7.00 | Over 65s: £7.00 | Benefit: £7.00

Rehearsal times: Tuesday evenings 7.00 pm - 9.00pm. Term dates: Autumn Term: Term 1: 15th September to 20th October; Term 2: 3rd November to 8th December.
events.summary: A no-audition community choir that learns folk, world and contemporary songs by ear, so there is no need to read music. Tuesday evenings in the Hall, across two autumn terms, conducted by folk singer Nonny Tabbush.
events.description:
Rehearsal times: Tuesday evenings 7.00 pm - 9.00pm

Term dates:

Autumn Term:

Term 1: 15th September to 20th October

Term 2: 3rd November to 8th December

Please ask to join the WhatsApp group on your first session to find out up-to-date information.

For all enquiries please email: admin@bristolfolkhouse.co.uk

Price: £7 per session (reduces to £6.50 per session if you block book more than 4 sessions)

A friendly choir based in the heart of Bristol. We learn songs by ear, so there's no need to read music. We don't hold auditions - come along, have a go, and give it a try. Singing in a choir is one of the simplest ways to feel good.

The choir will cover a wide variety of folk songs, as well as some world and contemporary music. This choir is happy and fun-loving, our aim is to create a sense of community and a love of singing.

If you fancy giving it a go, meeting some friendly people, and having a good sing then do come along. We meet at the Bristol Folk House in the Hall. The choir is conducted by Nonny Tabbush, a folk singer and choral practitioner. Nonny is a fun and lively choir conductor who has experience working with singers of all ages. She has started and run several community choirs, singing a range of materials including folk, world, and contemporary. She also works as a vocal practitioner for Bristol Plays Music, teaching songs in primary and secondary schools and she currently runs the Glox Vox choir in Bristol too.

Nonny is also an experienced performer, she started her career in vocal harmony when she was 16 years old, as one of The Tabbush Sisters, who performed at folk festivals across the country. She is now in a ceilidh band called The Bristol Ceilidh Quartet.

events.title: In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley
events.raw:
**In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley**

Tuesday 15th September 2026, 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

How can we really help autistic children in education?
events.summary: Neurodivergence campaigner Pete Wharmby and autism family consultant Lisa Galley on supporting autistic children at school and at home, with audience questions and a signing.
events.description:
We're delighted to host Pete Wharmby and Lisa Galley for a discussion on
education and care for autistic children.

In *Different Minds*, neurodivergence campaigner Pete Wharmby shines a light
on what it's like to be autistic in Western school systems today, so we can
understand how to support our children through the most important years of
their lives.

With gentle science, practical tools and deep validation, Lisa Galley's
*Parenting your Autistic Child* explains exactly what is happening in your
child's brain and body during these difficult moments — when they refuse to
get dressed, experience sensory overload or meltdown at 3.30pm — offering
practical strategies that work with their nervous system rather than against
it.

This informative and compassionate talk will be your chance to learn more,
ask questions and get copies of the books signed.

Peter Wharmby is a neurodivergence campaigner and former teacher who was
diagnosed autistic at age 34. He is also father to an autistic child.
Shocked by the statistics around depression, anxiety and life expectancy for
autistic people, Pete has immersed himself in working to improve
neurodiversity awareness and acceptance.

Lisa Galley is an Autism Family Consultant, and former Speech and Language
Therapist. She is also a dedicated mum to grown-up autistic kids. Her
mission is to empower parents of neurodivergent children to reject the
unrealistic neurotypical expectations that society places on autistic
children, and to embrace intuitive parenting that aligns with their unique
needs.

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**How Not to Save the World: Doing Good Without Annoying Everyone** —
Bookhaus

Wednesday 16th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.
events.summary: Anthea Lawson and Bristol organiser Liam Barrington-Bush on the blind spots of activism, and how to campaign without alienating the people you need to convince.
events.description:
Do you want to change the world but wonder if there's any point trying? Are
you unsure what you can offer, or don't feel that you fit the activist
mould? Do you think activists can be self-righteous, even oblivious to the
very people they're trying to help?

'A wise, rich and crucial book.' — George Monbiot

*How Not To Save the World* is a book about doing good, for anyone who has
looked at politics or public discourse and thought, 'we need better than
this.' The fervour that drives us to change the world can create blind
spots, where we don't see our own behaviour, or disregard it because the
cause is urgent.

Realistic, candid and hopeful, *How Not To Save the World* is a sympathetic
exploration of alternatives to righteousness, purity traps and other
unhelpful habits. It shows that there are ways to work together for what
matters, without alienating the people we need to convince.

We are delighted to welcome Anthea Lawson to bookhaus, where she will be in
conversation with Liam Barrington-Bush. Come and engage in a deep
conversation about activism and organising. Tickets are £7 and include a
glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

Anthea Lawson (she/her) is an author and campaigner. After training as a
journalist at The Times, she worked for campaign groups including Global
Witness and Amnesty International.

Liam Barrington-Bush (he/him) is a social movement facilitator, community
organiser and occasional writer. He lives in St Pauls, Bristol, is a
co-founder and co-director of RadHR, and started a community organising
workshop series called Embrace the Mess.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.title: Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon
events.raw:
When: 17 Sep – 2 Dec 2026

Official Planetarium Show from Pink Floyd, 10 tracks from The Dark Side of the Moon set
to cosmic 360° visuals.
events.summary: The authorised Dark Side of the Moon planetarium show — the album in full against 360-degree visuals, on an evening run into December.
events.description:
The Dark Side of the Moon returns to Bristol's Planetarium!

Celebrate over 50 years of Pink Floyd's legendary album The Dark Side of the Moon with a new
awe-inspiring audio-visual show.

Set to the newly remastered audio by James Guthrie and Joel Plante of das boot recording,
the sound is richer, deeper, and more powerful than ever. The breath-taking 360° visuals,
produced by the award-winning team at NSC Creative in collaboration with Pink Floyd's iconic
creative director Aubrey Powell, bring the music to life in spectacular style.

Each song has a different theme; some futuristically looking forward and some a retro
acknowledgment to Pink Floyd's visual history, all relating to a time and space experience,
embracing technology that only a Planetarium can offer.

So, join us for a truly immersive cosmic celebration of one of the greatest albums of all
time, now showing at the Planetarium.

**Autumn shows now available to book:** Thursday 17th Sept 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Friday 2nd
Oct 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Friday 6th Nov 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Thursday 26th Nov 6pm, 7:15pm,
8:30pm; Wednesday 2nd Dec 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm.

**Access considerations** — A hearing loop is available. Limited wheelchair spaces are
available, please book ahead. The Planetarium is a dark environment with a stepped walkway to
access seats. Planetarium shows can feature loud noises and flashing lights; visitors with
epilepsy and photosensitivity may suffer a seizure if exposed to flashing or strobe lighting.

**Planning your visit** — Doors open 20 minutes before start time. There will be a bar.
Tickets are checked at the entrance on Millennium Square next to the Planetarium. You can
explore the Space Gallery before being invited to enter the Planetarium. Please aim to arrive
at least 10 mins before your show; late entry will not be permitted.

events.summary: A three-hour introduction to kintsugi, the Japanese art of repairing broken ceramics — epoxy, natural urushi lacquer and a brass-powder gold finish. Suitable for complete beginners; morning and afternoon sittings.
events.description:
Learn the Japanese art of kintsugi repair for broken ceramics.

Spend the session immersed in the processes, tools and materials of
kintsugi and complete a repair using epoxy, coated with traditional
natural Japanese Urushi (tree sap) lacquer and finished to a stunning
gold-hued shine with fine brass powder.

Suitable for complete beginners. Materials and hot drinks are included.
Bring your own piece — small, under 20cm diameter, with simple breaks
into 2-3 pieces, open shapes like plates or dishes preferred — or
choose from pieces available on the day. The session covers epoxy,
epoxy putty, urushi and brass powder finishes.

£30 – £70, concessions available; your booking is secured with a £20
deposit. Two sittings on the day: 10:30–13:30 and 14:30–17:30.

events.summary: The shop launches an artist-in-residence strand in its window displays with CJ Reay of Black Lodge Press, fifteen years into a zine and print project rooted in radical history and DIY culture.
events.description:
Since taking over the bookshop a year ago we have been keen to begin
expanding our artistic and cultural offering further. Phil, our new
Co-Owner, is an Illustrator with strong links to artists and illustrators
around the country. The shop has great big window displays that have the
potential for displaying more visual art in all kinds of formats.

We are delighted to finally be launching this new program by welcoming Black
Lodge to bookhaus as our first artist in residence. We will be welcoming CJ
Reay, the person behind Black Lodge, to bookhaus for a conversation on his
artistic practices. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft
drink. Presented by bookhaus.

CJ Reay is an artist from Cumberland in the North West of England. Inspired
by autonomous movements, radical history and DIY culture he creates
agitational art in print and fabric. He's also one of the underground
horticulturists responsible for the Anarchist Gardeners Club. For the last
15 years he has operated Black Lodge Press; a publishing project putting out
zines, prints and other radical ephemera.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Andrew Maxwell Featuring Burt Williamson plus compere Jack Campbell

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly flagship comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ANDREW MAXWELL

The stupendous Andrew Maxwell headlines for The Comedy Box for the first time in decades. We first booked Andrew back in the 90s, then he grew a little too big for us. Now he’s back and we are proud to offer to you one of the best stand ups in the British Isles.

Throughout his long career, Andrew Maxwell has enjoyed many sell-out seasons at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe; he has also performed at The Amnesty / Channel Four’s Secret Policeman’s Ball (alongside Eddie Izzard, Chevy Chase and Dylan Moran), Glastonbury, The HBO US Comedy & Arts Festival in Las Vegas (alongside Jerry Seinfeld and Chris Rock), and made several appearances at the Montreal Just for Laughs Festival.

He was the special guest of friend Jim Jefferies for his Hammersmith Apollo dates in London. He is also a founder member of Altitude Comedy Festival, staged in the Alps. Andrew has recorded three Live DVDs with 2Entertain (Conflict Revolution, Andrew Maxwell: Live In Dublin & Andrew Maxwell: One Inch Punch).

**AS SEEN ON:**

Live At The Apollo (BBC One), Have I Got News For You (BBC One), Comedy Game Night, Never Mind the Buzzcocks, QI, The Secret Policeman’s Ball, I’m A Celebrity Get Me Out Of Here! (ITV) Celebrity Juice (ITV2) and Mock The Week (BBC Two). He is also the voice of Get Your Tats Out: Kavos Inc (Channel 5). Winner of King of Comedy.​

[Andrew Maxwell On Tour – Official Website](https://www.andrewmaxwellontour.com/)

#### “*One of the funniest men in Britain*” THE TELEGRAPH

#### “*Infuriatingly excellent*” THE SUNDAY TIMES

#### “*If you can only see one stand-up act, see Maxwell*” THE MIRROR

events.summary: Trump's eleven-day communications director turned critic brings his UK tour to St George's on the eve of the US midterms, with an audience Q&A. Booked through Intelligence Squared rather than the shop.
events.description:
This event is hosted by our partners at Intelligence Squared.

American democracy is on the brink. Masked agents menace the streets of
Minneapolis. Donald Trump jokes about cancelling elections. And traditional
allies like Canada and the UK are beginning to look for alliances that could
replace their pivotal relationships with the US.

According to Anthony Scaramucci, former White House Communications Director
turned outspoken Trump critic and host of The Rest is Politics: U.S.,
President Trump represents one of the most serious challenges the country
has faced.

This autumn, on the eve of the pivotal US midterm elections, Scaramucci
comes to live audiences across the UK to offer an insider's account of how
America reached this moment and to offer a hopeful message for how it might
find a way back. Drawing on his forthcoming book *All The Wrong Moves*, he
will trace a series of catastrophic decisions made by both Democrats and
Republicans that in Scaramucci's view dismantled decades of postwar
stability and prosperity. And he will describe how undoing these mistakes
can unlock a new era of success for America and the world.

Don't miss this opportunity to see Anthony Scaramucci — hilarious,
irreverent, insightful and deeply sourced within both the Republican and
Democratic parties — live in-person and ask your own questions in the
audience Q&A.

Tickets available through Intelligence Squared.

Big views to the Forest of Dean and a genuinely remote feel twenty minutes from Bristol.
events.description:
Leader: David Hawkins. Category: Botany. Date: 20th September 2026, 2:30 pm.

Littleton Warth offers a wide expanse of grazed saltmarsh, with fine views across
to the Forest of Dean and down to the Severn Bridge, and a remote, untamed
atmosphere. A good array of common saltmarsh plants should be visible in September
and the Warth supports a particularly large population of Slender Hare's-ear
*Bupleurum tenuissimum*, an anomalous and nationally scarce member of the carrot
family. Sea Clover *Trifolium squamosum* may prove harder to find amongst the
swathes of Strawberry Clover *Trifolium fragiferum*, and we may also be fortunate
enough to encounter a third nationally scarce species, the grass Bulbous Foxtail
*Alopecurus bulbosus*. With the seawall supporting a few common grassland plants
as well, there should be much to see.

Meet at car park at end of Whale Wharf Lane, ST588910 ///clincher.alive.begun,
nearest postcode BS35 1NP.

events.raw:
**The Mulai : Munir Hachemi**

Monday 21st September, Gloucester Road Books at 7.00 pm

The great Spanish author will be in conversation with author and academic,
Constantine Blintzios

[Book tickets](https://hdfst.uk/e160391) (this link will take you to
external site HeadFirst Bristol)
events.summary: The Granta Best of Young Spanish-Language Novelists pick discusses *The Mulai*, a Borges-inflected science fiction novel newly translated by Julia Sanches, with Constantine Blintzios.
events.description:
We're honoured to be hosting the great Spanish author and translator, Munir
Hachemi, who will be discussing his wonderful novel, *The Mulai*, in
conversation with the author, poet and creative writing teacher, Constantine
Blintzios.

*The Mulai*, newly translated from Spanish by Julia Sanches, is a wholly
original examination of language, identity and the fragile nature of
civilisations. Here's more from the novel's publisher, Fitzcarraldo
Editions:

> An archaeologist travels to a distant planet to spend time among a
> mysterious community, a people who live in temperature-controlled domes,
> worship a deity called Dog, and repeat an elliptical phrase from which
> they draw their name: mulai, the tree comes. The descendants of a
> long-forgotten space mission, the Mulai have abandoned the social norms
> that once bound them to Earth. Over centuries of isolation, their language
> has become more about change than stability, and the ways they eat, write,
> reproduce, bury their dead and understand gender have all transformed into
> something almost unrecognizable.

Drawing on Borges, Le Guin and Calvino, *The Mulai* is a mind-bending work
of metafiction whose interlocking puzzles resound with Munir Hachemi's
singularly playful and eclectic style.

Munir Hachemi's career as a writer began with them selling their stories in
the form of fanzines in the bars of the Lavapies neighbourhood of Madrid.
They are the author of *Living Things* and *The Mulai*, and are also a
translator from Chinese and English. In 2021, they appeared on Granta's Best
of Young Spanish-Language Novelists list.

address.street: Great Western Dockyard, Gas Ferry Road

events.raw:
21 September 2026

Meet real-life engineers, enjoy hands-on STEM activities, and discover Brunel's legacy at
our special Home Education Day.
events.summary: A day built for home-educating families — working engineers on site and hands-on STEM around Brunel's ship.
events.description:
Bristol Dockyards is home to the remarkable legacy of Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom
Brunel, but engineering is far from history. Join us this autumn for a special Home
Education Day where you can meet real-life engineers from Babcock and Bristol Dockyards,
discover what they do, and take part in hands-on STEM activities. You'll also have the
chance to learn more about Brunel and explore our newly opened museum dedicated to his
most famous ship, the SS Great Britain.

**What's included:** whole site access including the Brunel Institute, Being Brunel
Museum, SS Great Britain & NEW museum and Historic Dockyards.

**Key info** — Price: £9.00 pp; free for children 3 and under and carers accompanying a
paying disabled person. Date & time: Monday 21st September 2026, 10am-3pm.

**Additional bookable activities:**

- **Guided Tour of SS Great Britain** — Find out about the SS Great Britain's long and
  adventurous life, discover passengers and crew stories as you explore the ship with our
  knowledgeable volunteer tour guides. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, on board the ship, meeting at
  the stern. £2 per child, adults free but must be booked in.
- **Brunel's Big Ideas** (education workshop) — Take a closer look at some of Brunel's
  sketches, discover how the SS Great Britain was built then hunt for some of Brunel's
  engineering tools in one of our museums. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, Medlock classroom, Dry
  Dock and Being Brunel Museum. For children working at Key Stage 1 or 2. £3 per
  participating child, £1 per non-participating child, adults free.
- **Mission: Save the Ship** (education workshop) — Investigate the dehumidification system
  that protects the SS Great Britain and discover the science and engineering behind it
  with hands-on experiments led by the Ship's Conservation Engineer. 13:00-14:00, 60 mins,
  Medlock classroom and Dry Dock. For children aged 12+. £3 per participating child, £1 per
  non-participating child, adults free.

As the site is only open for home educating families it is likely to be quieter than it
would normally be at weekends or during school holidays. A covered picnic area with patio
heaters is available, and The Board Walk kiosk is open 8:30am-4:00pm.

events.title: A Way of Love launch with Peter Parker and Lurid Editions

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the books (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**A Way of Love launch with Peter Parker and Lurid Editions** — Bookhaus

Tuesday 22nd September, 18:30. Genres: workshops & classes, talks, lgbtq+.
events.summary: Peter Parker and Lurid Editions' D-M Withers on queer life before Stonewall, marking the first new edition of James Courage's 1959 novel *A Way of Love* alongside Parker's *Some Men in London*.
events.description:
Peter Parker and D-M Withers will be in conversation at bookhaus to
celebrate the publication of three books which provide insight into the
experiences and lives of gay men in the post-war, pre-Stonewall era.

Parker's critically acclaimed two volumes *Some Men in London: Queer Life
1945-59* and *1960-67* have just been published in paperback in the Penguin
Modern Classics series. *Some Men in London* features letters, diaries,
psychological textbooks, novels, films, plays and police records, covering a
wide range of viewpoints, from those who deplored homosexuality to those who
campaigned for its decriminalisation.

Parker's collections are the perfect companion piece to the latest reissue
from Bristol based indie Lurid Editions, *A Way of Love* by James Courage
(1903-1963). Originally published in 1959, Lurid's publication is the first
ever new edition of this important queer novel, written by a seriously
underappreciated author.

*A Way of Love* tells the story of the worldly architect Bruce Quantock and
his younger, inexperienced lover, Philip Dill. It is a beautifully written
novel set in the late '50s when queer communities were forced to live at
constant risk of blackmail or prison. Yet it also shows a thriving and
joyous subculture, and the defiant struggle gay men faced to live ordinary
lives, on their own terms.

Parker and Withers will discuss the life and times of James Courage, and
celebrate the career of this underappreciated mid-century author. Tickets
cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the books.
Presented by bookhaus.

D-M Withers is Director of Lurid Editions, a publisher of rediscovered queer
literature.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.
