events.title: The Disappearers: Marlon James
events.raw:
**The Disappearers : Marlon James**

Wednesday 23rd September, Lantern Hall, Bristol Beacon at 7.00 pm

One of the 21st century's most significant writers in conversation with
Vanessa Kisuule

[Book tickets](https://bristolbeacon.org/whats-on/marlon-james-priority/)
events.summary: The Booker winner brings *The Disappearers* to the Lantern Hall in conversation with Vanessa Kisuule — one of only four UK dates for the book.
events.description:
We are delighted to announce that we will be hosting Booker Prize winner and
one of the 21st century's most acclaimed novelists, Marlon James, in
September.

Marlon is coming to Bristol to introduce, discuss and read from his
hugely-anticipated new novel, *The Disappearers*, in what is one of only
four UK events the US-based author is undertaking for the book. He will be
in conversation with the celebrated author, poet and performer, Vanessa
Kisuule.

The novel marks a return to the territory of Marlon's brilliant Booker
winning, *A Brief History of Seven Killings*; the publication that fully
established him as an international literary star.

Set in late 1980s Kingston Jamaica, *The Disappearers* is an uncompromising,
acutely thought-provoking portrait of queer life in an often brutally
unaccepting society. Seven gay actors confront bigotry and hate following a
deadly attack at a rehearsal. Epic in its scale and awash with an
unbreakable humanity, the novel confirms Marlon James' place at the
forefront of modern fiction.

This is an unmissable opportunity to hear from one of the great writers of
our time.

events.title: Patricia Lockwood: Agate Head / Stone Soup

price.text: Price range: £8.00 through £19.00 (ticket only, or ticket plus a copy of the book)

events.raw:
**Patricia Lockwood: Agate Head / Stone Soup**

Wednesday 23rd September 2026, 6:30 pm

Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD

Price range: £8.00 through £19.00
events.summary: The author of *Priestdaddy* and *No One Is Talking About This* comes to North Street for the first time, marking a new poetry collection written alongside a second career as a metalsmith.
events.description:
Join us as we welcome a Storysmith all-time favourite, live in the shop for
the very first time! The one and only Patricia Lockwood, the original
Priestdaughter, will be in Bristol to mark the release of her new poetry
collection, *Agate Head / Stone Soup*, and in conversation about this
alongside other matters.

You may know Patricia from her life-defining memoir *Priestdaddy*, her
devastating yet delirious novels *No One Is Talking About This* (Storysmith
Book of the Year 2021) and *Will There Ever Be Another You*, her poetry
collection *Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals*, or that video where she
slowly extrudes a crystal egg from her mouth. We're very excited.

Pre-order your copy of *Agate Head / Stone Soup* (rrp £18.99) for a special
discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!

**About Agate Head / Stone Soup.** Many have called Patricia Lockwood a
wordsmith, but in the latest iteration of her life, she has become, quite
literally, a metalsmith too. Stones, gems, metals, fossils — she forges them
into bodies, faces and, with her typical irreverence, vaginas. In these
poems, a robot dog discovers the Lascaux caves in France. Jane Austen shoots
a perfect 147. A rock gets a girlfriend. Lockwood's most successful work of
metal- and wordsmithing yet is her blend of the Internet world with the
natural one, as she slips meme references and algospeak into evocations of
geological time.

events.raw: **Translated Fiction Book Club: 24/09 TWO YEAR BOOK CLUB ANNIVERSARY!** — £0.00.
events.summary: The translated fiction club turns two: a mini party and a discussion that revisits two years of reading.
events.description:
**Join us for an exciting evening to discuss translated literature. Whether you're a fan of literary fiction or just looking to try something new, this book club hopes to achieve just that. **

**In September, we'll be celebrating our book club's two year anniversary! Come along for a mini party and book club discussion that takes a trip down memory lane...**

***Date:***

Thursday 24th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us via info@maxminervas.co.uk.

All you have to do is read the book and show up on the night.

**THE TWO YEAR BOOK CLUB SPECIAL:**

To celebrate the book club's two year anniversary, we're going to take a trip down memory lane and revisit the books we've explored together in our book club.

The goal is simple: pick your favourite book club title and bring it on the night so we can discuss what we all liked, didn't like, and see what titles we're all fond of.

*Eligible books:*

- ***Brandy Sour*** by Constantia Soteriou, translated from Greek by Lina Protopapa (Cyprus)

- ***Elevator in **Sài Gòn*** by Thuận, translated from Vietnamese by Nguyễn An Lý (Vietnam)

- ***Down the Rabbit Hole*** by Juan Pablo Villalobos, translated from Spanish by Rosalind Harvey (Mexico)

- ***The Vegetarian*** by Han Kang, translated from Korean by Deborah Smith (South Korea)

- ***Ceasaria*** by Hanna Nordenhök, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Sweden)

- ***Spanish Beauty*** by Esther García Llovet, translated from Spanish by Richard Village (Spain)

- ***Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead*** by Olga Tokarzcuk, translated from Polish by Antonia Lloyd-Jones (Poland)

- ***The National Telepathy*** by Roque Larraquy, translated from Spanish by Frank Wynne (Argentina)

- ***On the Calculation of Volume I ***by Solvej Balle, translated from Danish by Barbara J Haveland (Denmark)

- ***From Savagery ***by Alejandra Banca, translated from Spanish by Katie Brown (Venezuela)

- ***The Little I Knew ***by Chiara Valerio, translated from Italian by Ailsa Wood (Italy)

- ***Just A Little Dinner*** by Cécile Tili, translated from French by Katherine Gregor (France)

- ***The Memory Police*** by Yoko Ogawa, translated from Japanese by Stephen Snyder (Japan)

- ***Heart Lamp ***by Banu Mushtaq, translated from Kannada by Deepa Bhasti (India)

- ***On the Calculation of Volume II ***by Solvej Balle, translated from Danish by Barbara J Haveland (Denmark)

- ***Chess*** by Stefan Zweig, translated from German by Anthea Bell (Austria)

- ***The Palace on the Higher Hill*** by Karim Kattan, translated from French by Jeffrey Zuckerman (Palestine)

- ***Sánchez ***by Esther García Llovet, translated from Spanish by Richard Village (Spain)

- ***The Rarest Fruit*** by Gaëlle Bélem, translated from French by Karen Fleetwood and Laëtitia Saint-Loubert (Réunion)

- ***The Love of Singular Men*** by Victor Heringer, translated from Portuguese by James Young (Brazil)

- ***Before The Rocket ***by Loranne Vella, translated from Maltese by Kat Storace (Malta)

- ***Cathedrals*** by Claudia Piñeiro, translated from Spanish by Frances Riddle (Argentina)

- ***Taiwan Travelogue ***by Yáng Shuāng-zǐ, translated from Mandarin by Lin King (Taiwan)

- ***She Who Remains ***by Rene Karabash, translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel (Bulgaria)

"The book club was born out of a love for translated literature and a desire to find a community. When I started the book club two years ago, I had no idea that it would have become so integral to my routine. We've had the pleasure of welcoming translators, new faces, and discussing books from 22 different countries together. I hope to keep reading around the world with you all for many more years! Thank you for everything." - Ev

price.text: £29 includes a copy of the book / £5 admission only

events.raw:
**An Evening with Jonn Elledge**

Thursday 24th September 2026, 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

From electric lighting to pedestrian crossings
events.summary: The author of *A History of the World in 47 Borders* on *31 Inventions that Built Our World* — lifts, street lighting, parks, pedestrian crossings — with a Q&A and signing.
events.description:
For over 10,000 years, we humans have been busy altering our environment and
embracing 'progress', evolving seamlessly from hunter gatherers to the
modern urban sophisticates we see ourselves as today.

But what are the ideas and inventions that enabled humanity to become, by
the early 21st century, a majority urban species for the first time? How did
the essential infrastructure of modern life — the innovations that we barely
even notice, but without which our world would fall apart — actually come to
be?

With his characteristic wit and boundless curiosity, Jonn Elledge invites us
to join him on a fascinating and often surprising tour of the ideas and
technologies that made modernity possible. From elevators to electric
lighting, parks to pedestrian crossings, he guides us through the history of
civilisation itself.

Jonn will talk about his new book before an audience Q&A and book signing.

events.description:
Have you ever thought that moths are just drab butterflies? That the only thing
they do is eat holes in your clothes? This 2-part crash course in moths will
prove you wrong!

Part one, online, Friday 25 September 2026, 6:00pm–7:00pm: the variety of
moths, how they differ from butterflies, their ecological importance, and
practical trap-setting techniques.

Part two, in person, Saturday 26 September 2026, 9:00am–10:30am: observing the
captured specimens and practising identification.

This event is part of our Youth Programme so we ask anyone attending to be
between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome. Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road,
Bristol, BS16 1EL.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***BIG LITTLE TRUTHS***

After the lies, come the truths . . .

Ten years ago, at the Pirriwee High School gates, the friendships of Celeste, Jane and Madeline were forged in the fires of young motherhood, the big little lies we all tell to hide our deepest fears and secrets – and the event that changed everything.

Now mothers to hormonal teens, these frazzled friends are starting to worry about the strangers newly occupying their kids’ bedrooms. Or they would, if they weren’t so distracted by their own problems. Because Madeline’s landmark birthday is about to land a bombshell. Jane’s rock-solid marriage is suddenly crumbling. And Celeste’s mother-in-law is asking awkward questions about the past. Not to mention the mystery of who sent the school receptionist a freshly severed finger. So many difficult little truths that each is facing.

Such a pity then that not a one of them can see the biggest ugliest truth hiding in their midst . . .

***Big Little Truths is the sequel to Big Little Lies, the breakout worldwide phenomenon that has sold over 6 million copies and is an Emmy- and Golden Globe-winning HBO sensation, produced by and starring Reese Witherspoon and Nicole Kidman. This novel follows Madeline, Celeste and Jane and their teenage kids years later, and will inspire the upcoming TV series.***

**ABOUT THE AUTHORS**

**Liane Moriarty** is the bestselling author of ten novels, including *Here One Moment*, *Apples Never Fall, The Husband's Secret, Big Little Lies* and *Nine Perfect Strangers*. Her novels have sold more than 25 million copies worldwide and have been translated into over 40 languages. *Big Little Lies* is now an Emmy and Golden Globe-winning HBO series, produced by and starring Nicole Kidman and Reese Witherspoon. *Nine Perfect Strangers* and *Apples Never Fall* have both been adapted for TV. *Here One Moment* is being adapted for TV by Nicole Kidman and Bruna Papandrea. Liane lives in Sydney with her husband, son and daughter.

**Charlotte Philby** is a critically acclaimed author of six novels. As a journalist, she worked for eight years as a newspaper reporter, editor and columnist at the *Independent*, where she was shortlisted for the Cudlipp Prize for investigative reporting. She is a former contributing editor and features writer at *Marie Claire*, and has written for publications including the *Sunday Times, New Statesman* and *Financial Times*. With the support of the BFI, she is currently adapting for film her novel *Edith and Kim*, which reimagines the lives of her grandfather, the double-agent Kim Philby, and Edith Tudor-Hart, who recruited him to the Soviet cause. Charlotte has three children and lives in Bristol.

Relax, play and have fun together in our Play Friday sessions for under 5s and their
grown-ups.

Each month, our Theatre of Curiosity space comes alive with a different mini-adventure
developed specially for our youngest visitors.

Our Play Friday sessions are developed using the theory of schematic play to encourage
open-ended exploration and help children learn about the world through play.

**Upcoming events:** 25 Sept, 6 Nov, 4 Dec.

September's theme is 'On A Roll'. It's time to twist, turn, spin and roll. Experiment with
spinning tops and rolling toys or turn yourself around. This session is based on the Rotation
Schema: where a child is fascinated by objects or their own body spinning, twisting, rolling,
or moving in circles. It helps toddlers and young children develop balance, coordination,
spatial awareness, and an understanding of cause and effect.

events.description:
### Stand Up For The Weekend with Mike Gunn Featuring Michelle Shaughnessy plus compere Jeremy Flynn

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: MIKE GUNN

Widely regarded as one of the UK’s finest circuit comedians, Mike Gunn blends darkly intelligent observations with a brilliantly understated delivery, finding humour in family life, middle age and the everyday frustrations we can all relate to. A misspent youth and a series of grim jobs cultivated his cynical outlook on life and a perverse desire led him to the world of stand-up. A self-confessed pessimist, he describes himself as “not a natural choice for a career in laughter”. He has a rare ability to walk close to the line of what audiences find acceptable and yet still remain likable and funny. His reputation for being a bit unfriendly, a touch dark and even morose is really not true. In real life he’s loving, warm and philanthropic. Just a bit misunderstood.

#### “*Piercingly funny… fiendishly funny, as dry as a dead man’s bones*.” — The List

#### “*There is plenty of enjoyment to be had in his downbeat meanderings on the futility of life*.” Chortle

#### “*Mike Gunn will make you die laughing*.” — The Guardian

#### Highly Commended Comedy Award — Time Out Dubai

[https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/](https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/)

surreal, compassionate, existential, vulgar, elegant, very funny, and very
sad. I love it.' — Dame Sheila Hancock

In *Pea Green Boat*, Stewart Lee and David Waywell create a dark, grotesque
retelling of *The Owl and the Pussycat* in which Edward Lear's characters
are revealed to be catastrophically poorly-equipped for maritime travel.
Told through the increasingly deranged diary of the Owl, the real story is
unmasked — he cannot open the honey jar due to his lack of opposable thumbs,
he is terrified the cat will eat him in his sleep, and he struggles to play
the guitar despite having no fingers.

Inspired by the cult 2001 stage piece, *Pea Green Boat* blends Lee's
fascination with Edward Lear with his own comedy. Now, with David's
gothic-comic illustrations, the story is brought vividly, hilariously and
unsettlingly to life.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.title: Mark Thomas – 40 in Stand-Up Years
events.raw:
**Comedy: Mark Thomas – 40 IN STAND-UP YEARS** —
Sep 30, 8:00 pm - 10:00 pm, Hen & Chicken Studio.
events.summary: Mark Thomas's fortieth-anniversary show. Its permalink contains a typo the venue has left in place (/copmedy-...), and it is date-scoped, unlike every other row.
events.description:
What?! Mark Thomas has been ‘standing up’ for 40 years? Impossible!! But how old does that make you…? Alas it is true; one of our oldest surviving alternative comics celebrates 40 years at the mic.

So, here’s what he has done so far in numbers; performed comedy for 40 years, won 8 awards for performing, 4 for human rights work and 1 he invented for himself, made 6 series of the Mark Thomas Comedy Product (Channel 4), written 6 books and 5 play scripts, made 5 series of the Manifesto for Radio 4, made 3 Dispatches for Channel 4, sued the police (and won) 3 times, curated and authored 2 art exhibitions with artist Tracey Moberly and had 1 Guinness World Record for holding 20 protests in 24 hours.

If that’s not enough, he’s also walked 724km around the length of the Israel Wall in the West Bank, been credited with changing the law on tax avoidance, started a comedy club in Palestine with Dr Sam Beale and campaigned successfully for things like trade union recognition for cinema workers and getting multinationals to change their practices. You’re right, there’s more, but your attention is running out and we’re running out of space. So let’s just say he’s generally mucked about trying to have fun and upset the right people…which he is really, really good at.

So basically expect a taster menu of government and personal mayhem, jokes, rants and a personal state of the nation broadcast as he tries to turn ‘what the f*ck is going on’ into a cogent hour of stand-up.

★★★★★ “*Once again shooting laughter-laden political bullets from the lip*” THE RECS

events.summary: Carey Marx headlines the Saturday club night.
events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Carey Marx & Guests Featuring Joey Page plus compere Jack Campbell

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

#### Headliner: CAREY MARX

Carey Marx is an unapologetic gagsmith. The jokes are short and sharp, often uncomfortably so, as any morality is sacrificed on the altar of quick laughs. And there’s no better way of guaranteeing a reaction than storming headlong into decidedly dodgy territory.

There’s plenty here for the connoisseur of comedy writing. The lines are efficient, original and potent – and rarely fail to blindside the audience.

And they come at a blistering rate, thanks to a hugely economical delivery. He doesn’t go out of the way to befriend an audience, yet there is a subtle charm and intelligence to him, even when the material is blatantly offensive.

#### “*Hilariously demented*” Edinburgh Evening News

#### “*Anecdotally debauched … But if his lines are frequently sick, they’re elegantly written, too, and there’s a childlike glee to his naughtiness*.” The Herald

https://www.facebook.com/CareyMarxComedy/

# Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 – The Toolbox

This introductory woodworking course teaches students to create a
softwood toolbox with a handle and inset base using traditional hand
tools and corner rebate joints. Upon completion, participants take
home their finished toolbox and gain foundational skills to pursue
home projects or advance to Level 2 classes.

**LEARN HOW TO:**

- Sawing straight and square
- Accurately marking out and cutting joints
- Effectively using hand tools including chisels and planes
- Fitting and finishing woodwork projects

**Skill level:** "Suitable for those with no previous woodwork
experience or, more experienced woodworkers wanting to improve their
skills and accuracy."

**Course options available:**

1. Thursday or Friday Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 3:40pm
2. Tuesday Evening Classes — 6:20pm to 8:45pm
3. Weekend Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 4:40pm

admired performers and creative voices."

events.raw: **Event 06/10: An evening with David McKay, award-winning translator** — From £6.00.
events.summary: What it takes to carry a Dutch novel into English, with David McKay on his translation of Anjet Daanje's The Song of Stork and Dromedary.
events.description:
**We are absolutely delighted to be hosting David McKay, the award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and non-fiction, who will be discussing his latest translation of Anjet Daanje's *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*. This will be a fantastic and riveting evening spent discussing what it takes to bring a Dutch novel into English.**

**Date:**
Tuesday 6th of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£25 ticket with The Song of Stork and Dromedary (hardback)
£12.99 ticket with The Remembered Soldier (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOKS**

***The Song of Stork and Dromedary***

**Inspired by the life and work of Emily Brontë, this masterful, multi-award-winning book — acclaimed as the best Dutch novel published this century — pulls readers into a narrative that redefines time itself.**

In the early 1800s, in Yorkshire, Eliza May Drayden and her sisters live far from the public eye, devoted to their shared love of reading and writing books. When, after dozens of rejections, Eliza May’s only novel, *Haeger Mass*, is finally published, it’s labelled as ‘ghastly’ and ‘immoral’. Over time, however, it is embraced by generations of readers as a masterpiece, and tales about its mysterious, reclusive author take on a life of their own.

In eleven extraordinary chapters, the story of Eliza May — both before and after her death — unfolds: through the tales of people who met her; her sister’s letters; her biographers’ words; the pages of a mysterious notebook; and the lives that become intertwined with hers, even centuries later.

In *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*, Anjet Daanje has crafted an absorbing literary mystery and an unforgettable meditation on love, life, loss, and the inexplicable nature of time. As the Brontës themselves did, Daanje shows us that storytelling is our only way to transcend death.

***The Remembered Soldier***

**An extraordinary love story and a captivating novel about the power of memory and imagination.**

Flanders 1922. After serving as a soldier in the Great War, Noon Merckem has lost his memory and lives in a psychiatric asylum. Countless women, responding to a newspaper ad, visit him there in the hope of finding their spouse who vanished in battle. One day a woman, Julienne, appears and recognises Noon as her husband, the photographer Amand Coppens, and takes him home against medical advice. But their miraculous reunion doesn’t turn out the way that Julienne wants her envious friends to believe. Only gradually do the two grow close, and Amand’s biography is pieced together on the basis of Julienne’s stories about him. But how can he be certain that she’s telling the truth?

In *The Remembered Soldier*, Anjet Daanje immerses us in the psyche of a war-traumatised man who has lost his identity. When Amand comes to doubt Julienne’s word, the reader is caught up in a riveting spiral of confusion that only the greatest works of literature can achieve.

*Longlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.*

**ABOUT THE TRANSLATOR**

**David McKay** is an award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and nonfiction. Born and educated in the United States, he has lived in and around The Hague since 1997.

In October, we'll be delving into *Drayton and McKenzie by Alexander Starritt*, a Sunday Times, GQ, and Financial Times 2025 Book of the Year. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 7th of October

Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *Drayton and McKenzie***

**A TIMES/SUNDAY TIMES, GQ, FINANCIAL TIMES AND BLOOMBERG BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR 2025**

*‘A big, bustling novel about love, friendship, money, ambition and the 21st century, packed with humour and intelligent observations … I finished it tear-stained’ Sunday Times*

*‘Will have you hooked … an ode to the enduring power of male friendship’ The Times Best Summer Books*

*‘My book of the summer’ Janice Turner*

*‘Thrilling’ Guardian*

For the first time since university, James and Roland’s paths through life – one drawn in straight lines, the other squiggled and meandering – began to cross…

James Drayton has always found things too easy. By the time he leaves university, he’s still waiting for a challenge worthy of his ambitions. Roland Mackenzie, on the other hand, is an impulsive risk-taker, a charismatic drifter with a knack for derailing his own attempts to get started in life.

When a chance encounter in a pub reunites these old acquaintances, it sets them on an unpredictable course through the upheavals of the twenty-first century, and sparks an unlikely alliance. Sent to Aberdeen during the financial crisis to lay off hundreds of workers, James and Roland begin to wonder: what if they were made for more than this? What if together they could build something grand and lasting – something that might even change the world?

price.text: Price range: £8.00 through £20.00; ticket types include an event ticket only (low income) option

events.raw:
**Meg Mason: Sophie, Standing There**

Thursday 8th October 2026, 7pm

The Station, Silver Street, Bristol, BS1 2AG

Price range: £8.00 through £20.00
events.summary: The author of *Sorrow and Bliss* on her new novel about loneliness and parasocial love, in conversation with Monica Heisey. Moved out of the shop to The Station, with a low-income ticket available.
events.description:
We are delighted to welcome the international bestselling author of the
seminal novel *Sorrow and Bliss*, Meg Mason, to Bristol this autumn! She'll
be here to discuss her new novel *Sophie, Standing There* with fellow author
and chronicler of life's ineffable difficulties, Monica Heisey (author of
equally-beloved bestseller *Really Good Actually*, writer on Schitt's
Creek).

*Sorrow and Bliss* won Book of the Year at the British Book Awards, was
shortlisted for the Women's Prize, and has been translated into more than 30
languages. *Sophie, Standing There* is one of the most anticipated books of
the year, and has already won praise from Gillian Anderson and Ann Patchett
(no biggie).

Pre-order your copy of *Sophie, Standing There* (rrp £20.00) for a special
discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!

**About the book.** Sophie Pattison is a lovely person — warm, kind,
relentlessly positive. She's cherished by her brother Laurie, adored by her
best friend Emma and valued by her colleagues. Sometimes, it's true, one day
in her life can feel like the entire month of January. It's also true she
can go an entire day without speaking. But she's fine really. She spends her
time alone reading, finding comfort in the pages of the books she devours.
Until one day she stumbles upon an author she hasn't read in years. Her
books, interviews and podcasts soon become a lifeline; every word is a
solace, company she hasn't felt in so long. It's almost like love.

**Venue access.** Access information for The Station is linked from the
event page.

events.title: Planetarium Nights: Light from Afar 3D
events.raw:
When: 8 Oct – 17 Dec 2026
Where: Planetarium
Recommended for: Adults. 16+

Discover the ways we explore the universe in our latest in-depth science planetarium show
for adults.
events.summary: The newest adult Planetarium Nights show, on the instruments and methods by which we actually see the universe.
events.description:
How about a trip to the stars on your Thursday night? Planetarium Nights are back this
Autumn!

Discover how astronomers capture the light from distant objects with advanced telescopes in
our revamped science show. Investigate how that light is used to calculate the scale of the
cosmos and to find alien worlds. Join us in the Planetarium to explore our galaxy… and
beyond!

**Highlights:**

- Where is the best place to go stargazing? And how do astronomers see beyond the haze of
  Earth's atmosphere?
- How can we read the fingerprints in the light? And what do they tell us about alien worlds?
- How many galaxies are in the Universe? And how can we work it out by studying one patch of
  sky?

**Upcoming events:** Oct 8 - 6pm; Oct 22 - 7:15pm; Nov 5 - 6pm; Nov 19 - 7:15pm; Dec 3 -
6pm; Dec 17 - 7:15pm.

Looking for more stargazing and floating through space? Check out our seasonal stargazing
show 'The Story of Stars'.

events.raw:

events.summary: An adults-only evening in the dome on how stars live and die, including our own sun's ending.
events.description:
How about a trip to the stars on your Thursday night? Planetarium Nights are back this
Autumn!

Join us for our seasonal stargazing show, where our team of presenters will take you on a
journey through the solar system to discover the winter night sky above us.

**Highlights:**

- Gaze up at a real-time, accurate map of Bristol's night sky, to uncover what you can see
  that night and investigate the secrets hidden in some well known constellations.
- Witness the majestic life-cycle of star, from humble nebula to exploding supernova.
- Dance on the edge of a black hole, with a 3D view like no other.

**Upcoming events:** Oct 8 - 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Oct 22 - 6pm, 8:30pm; Nov 5 - 7:15pm, 8:30pm;
Nov 19 - 6pm, 8:30pm; Dec 3 - 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Dec 17 - 6pm, 8:30pm.

events.title: Geology 1979 Reunion
events.venueName: University of Bristol — alumni and public events
events.raw: **Geology 1979 Reunion** — 9 October 2026, 12.00 PM - 10 October 2026, 5.00 PM. Venue: TBC.
events.summary: Geologists who started in 1979 mark fifty years over two days: Friday lunch, the Geology Department and the Wills Building tower, then on Saturday either the rediscovered caverns under the Clifton Suspension Bridge with a geologist guide, or a walking tour of St Nicholas Market. The venue is still to be confirmed.
events.description:
The Geologists of 1979 are delighted to invite you to a reunion on 9 and 10 October 2026, celebrating 50 years since they started the course.

Their plans include meeting for lunch on the Friday, followed by a visit to the Geology Department and a tour of the Wills Building including a trip up the tower, followed by an evening meal in a restaurant in Bristol.

On Saturday morning there are the possibilities of a trip down to the caverns below the Clifton suspension bridge (only rediscovered about 20 years ago) with a guide who is a geologist or a walking tour of St Nicks market (they will do a poll once they know who is able to come).

Please forward this invitation to any friends who graduated in 1979 that you are still in touch with.

**Contact**

If you are interested in coming, please email the organiser, John Leeson (BSc Geology 1979) at johnleeson@aol.com. Further details will be communicated closer to the time.

This event is organised by alumni volunteers and is independent of the University of Bristol. The University of Bristol does not accept any liability for this event.

events.summary: Neuroscience and psychology researchers on 150 years of brain research at Bristol, held on the eve of the University's 150th birthday and doubling as a first look inside the new Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus. Free, with refreshments afterwards.
events.description:
Join us for an exclusive evening celebrating 150 years of pioneering brain
research at the University of Bristol. Held on the eve of the University's
150th birthday, this special event offers alumni and supporters the chance
to be among the first to experience the new Temple Quarter Enterprise
Campus.

Hear from leading academics as they explore exciting advances in
Neuroscience and Psychology, from memory to movement, and discuss the
discoveries shaping the future of human health and wellbeing. Afterwards,
enjoy refreshments, reconnect with fellow alumni and explore Bristol's
newest campus.

As an alumnus, you are an important part of Bristol's story of innovation,
ambition and hope. Join us to celebrate the past and future of research on
campus.

This event showcasing the best of Bristol research has been made possible
with generous funding from the Bristol Collegiate Research Society.

**Schedule**

- 6:30 pm - 7:00 pm: Registration opens
- 7:00 pm - 08:30 pm: Bristol and the Brain discussion begins
- 8:30 pm - 9:30 pm: Networking and Food
- 10:00 pm: Event close

events.raw:
**An Evening with Jack Shoulder - Book Launch & Exhibition**

Friday 9th October 2026, 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

An event of art and handsomeness
events.summary: The *Museum Bums* co-author launches *Hotties in Art*, a tour of art history by way of its most alluring subjects, surrounded by a one-night pop-up exhibition of work by local artists.
events.description:
Has an artwork ever made you hot under the collar? How often have you walked
through a gallery, tried to focus on the text panel, but, really, just been
enamoured by the drop dead gorgeous guy staring back at you?

Offering a fresh and humorous introduction to art and written by *Museum
Bums* co-author Jack Shoulder, this book searches art history, across
movements and throughout the world to find the most alluring artworks — some
famous while others rarely ever seen before. Whether you are looking for
boyfriend material, a heavenly hunk, a bright young thing or even holding
out for a hero, there is a Museum Hottie carefully curated for you.

We're delighted to welcome Jack to discuss this new funny, informative and
eye candy-filled book!

To make this event even more special, we are looking to feature artwork
pieces by local artists on the night as a pop-up exhibition to surround Jack
during his event. So whether you're a professional or amateur illustrator,
painter, sculptor or sketcher, we'd love to hear from you — please email the
shop for more details.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

## Stand Up For The Weekend with Michael Shafar & Guests Featuring Jamie D’Souza plus compere Meryl O’Rourke

#### Headliner: MICHAEL SHAFAR

Originally from Melbourne, Michael Schafar is now based in London where he has quickly become one of the most exciting new acts on the UK comedy circuit. He regularly performs at the country’s biggest clubs where he gets to mock British people for their awful history and terrible food to their faces.​​

If you have lived in Australia, or even just visited there, you might already know Michael from his appearances on Network 10’s The Project and Studio 10, ABC’s Comedy Bites and triple j’s Good Az Friday. Of course, traditional media is dead, so it’s more likely that you might be one of his 100,000+ followers on social media or the 100+ million people who have seen his videos online. You may have also watched his debut special A(LIVE) on Amazon Prime or his most recent special Alright, Next Joke on YouTube.​

[BIO | Michael Shafar](https://www.michaelshafar.com/bio)

#### “*Shafar circumnavigates the line between edgy and offensive with beautiful finesse*” The Age (Melbourne)

#### “*He’s a brand of comedian that is getting rarer and rarer to come by these days, and if you’re among those who fear comedy has gotten too politically correct, this show will put those fears to rest*.” Time Out

#### “*Shafar has a disarmingly relaxed approach and an intelligent sense of humour with a wildly inventive, darkly comic imagination*.” The Edinburgh Reporter

events.summary: The UK's flight-sim show returns after six years, taking over the museum for a weekend of software, hardware, workshops and landing challenges.
events.description:
The biggest UK Flight Simulation event of 2026 is landing at Aerospace Bristol!

After six years, the UK is once again hosting its very own flight simulation show and it’s
happening here at Aerospace Bristol. Headlined by Platinum Sponsors MOZA and iniBuilds,
the event will showcase some of the biggest names in flightsim software development and
hardware innovation.

FSimUK will take place over two days with plenty to keep you occupied throughout. Whether
you’re a casual desktop flyer, a hardcore cockpit builder, a pilot in the making or an
interested bystander, this will be an unmissable weekend.

Visit https://fsimuk.bfsg.club for more information and to reserve your free goody bag.

**What to expect?**

- Discover the latest software and hardware from some of the best in the industry.
- Speak to the experts for advice on building or extending your own flightsim environment.
- Find out what’s happening behind the scenes at the FSElite stage in the John James
  Theatre.
- Get to the top of the leader board in the landing challenges to nab yourself a prize.
- Join hands-on workshops for tutorials and demonstrations.

Remember! Annual ticket holders can visit for free with a valid ticket. You can visit at
anytime between 10am-5:30pm.

events.description:
Join us for a special Black History Month screening of The Six Triple
Eight, the remarkable true story of the only all-Black, all-female
battalion to serve overseas during World War II. Against the odds, these
trailblazing women overcame discrimination and adversity to make a
lasting impact on history.

Come and be inspired by this powerful story of courage, resilience, and
determination. Don't miss this opportunity to celebrate and reflect on
the extraordinary contributions of these pioneering women.

Settle in with a cup of tea and make yourself a delicious toastie
sandwich while you watch.

This is a free event, and all are welcome.

Location: Purdown View, MOVE Studio, Frenchay Campus, Coldharbour Lane,
Bristol BS16 1QY.

Accessibility: disabled parking on campus, step-free access, automatic
doors, accessible toilets, guide and assistance dog friendly, quiet
spaces available. No induction loop.

events.description:
Don’t miss the all-new show from Scotland’s hilarious new stand-up superstar who is widely hailed as one of the most exciting breakthrough artists in the global live comedy scene.

A social media sensation with 100’s of millions of online views, FLOW is Connor Burns’ 5th solo show – an hour of new standup featuring his intelligent and razor-sharp wit, brilliant jokes and his now-signature, single-malt level of Scottish cynicism that blends perfectly with his relatable everyman take on life, and which in 2025, won him the coveted Forth Fringe Award.

Connor sold more than 17,000 tickets for FLOW’s premiere at the 2026 Edinburgh Fringe – before the festival even started! The massive demand for tickets saw him add three extra shows at the 3000 seat Edinburgh Playhouse – the UK’S largest purpose-built theatre – in addition to his full fringe run. His last tour GALLUS also sold huge numbers of seats, added encore dates UK-wide and finished up with a record breaking five sold-out shows in the flagship King’s Theatre during 2026’s Glasgow International Comedy Festival.

He tours extensively across the UK, Australia, Europe, and off-Broadway in 2024 and 2025 as part of the prestigious Fringe Encore Series and the New York Comedy Festival. He released 2 comedy specials GALLUS and Vertigo* (*on comedy powerhouse 800LB Gorilla)

We say all this because you haven’t seen Connor on UK television – no panel shows, no chat shows, no stand-up showcases. It’s all happening as a result of his hilarious live shows and laugh-out-loud social media clips so we are incredibly excited to welcome Connor back to Bristol’s Hen & Chicken – book your tickets fast!

**Emerson's Green** — 11.10.2026, 2:00 pm. Leader: David Hawkins. Category: Botany.

"An exciting chance to make some significant records in an extremely under-recorded
part of town. The monad (1km OS map grid square) that we will target currently has
just a single record to its name in the Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland's
database: Fine-leaved Sandwort *Sabulina tenuifolia*. And what's more, that record
was made in 1898 by none other than the great J. W. White, author of the seminal
The Bristol Flora."

"Meet on Emerson's Green Common just off Emerson's Green Lane at ST668768
///events.ears.brave. Postcode BS16 7HB."
events.summary: Recording botany in a Bristol kilometre square that has exactly one record against it — made in 1898 by J. W. White, who wrote The Bristol Flora. David Hawkins is fairly sure the sandwort he found has gone, and equally sure the afternoon will turn up something. The one meeting on the programme actually inside the city.

events.summary: A movement and clowning show for babies and toddlers up to three, touring early years settings and community spaces across the South West through late October. Ninety minutes including a gentle start and a break; individual tour dates were still unannounced when the page was read.
events.description:
What does that first step feel like? How does interacting with someone else make us feel? Why does rolling over feel so good!

Join us as we journey from 0-3 years old, finding our feet, our feelings and our fun. Find a connection whether you have children of your own, or from when you yourself were a child.

Using movement and clowning, *Wonder Baby* invites children and families to explore physical play and experience the joy of creating space to play together.

Grown from the imaginations and experiences of babies, toddlers and their families – *Wonder Baby* was developed in collaboration with families who took part in the early development of the show.

For 0-3's and their families.

**Duration:** This is a play and performance experience, lasting approximately 90 minutes - this includes a gentle start and time for a break if needed.

**At A Glance:** 11 - 29 October 2026. Various early years settings and community spaces across the South West. Suitable for 0-3's and their families and carers. No public tickets currently available. We will be announcing tour dates in early September.

events.timesText: 7:30 pm - 9:30 pm, in the Chicken Shed
events.raw:
**Comedy: Wednesday Night Improv**

14 October · 19:30 – 21:30 · From £6
events.summary: Two halves of unscripted comedy in the Chicken Shed: audience-prompted improv games, then a guest two-prov set.
events.description:
Wednesday Night Improv returns to the Hen & Chicken with two halves of unscripted comedy – all made up on the spot, all inspired by your suggestions. Expect quick wit, bold characters, and the kind of laughter that only happens when nobody knows what’s coming next (including the performers).

**## FIRST HALF ##Comedy Games, Improvised Live**

*(Think Whose Line Is It Anyway? meets Game Changer, with a sprinkling of Taskmaster.)*

A fast, funny first half built around short improvised games – the kind where performers get a prompt from the audience and have seconds to turn it into something brilliant. Points will be awarded. Consequences may follow.

With your host, Ste Brown.

**## SECOND HALF ##The BLANK Who BLANKED Me**

Love stories are with us from a very young age, usually stories of love that is pure and sweet and true. *The BLANK who BLANKED me* is not that kind of love story.

This is the kind of love story where passion strikes like a wrecking ball, leaving you dazed, confused, and madly in love with an unaccountable asshole who does admittedly look really good climbing out of a lake in a thin white shirt…

—

Whether you’re a seasoned comedy fan or just curious about what happens when performers make it all up as they go, this is a perfect night to dive into Bristol’s thriving improv scene. Expect laughter, surprises, and something completely different — every single time.

—

*Part of the Wednesday Night Improv series – second Wednesday of every month.* *Details: https://linktr.ee/wednightimprov*

when there is a reduced sensory environment – particularly neurodivergent people of all

events.summary: A reduced-sensory opening of the whole site, run for neurodivergent visitors and anyone else who needs it quieter.
events.description:
Calm Sensory Sessions have been designed for anyone who benefits from visiting at a time
when there is a calmer background sensory environment – particularly neurodivergent people
of all ages.

**What will the sessions include?** We understand that the sensory experience at SS Great
Britain can be challenging for some of our visitors. Where possible these calm sensory
sessions will include:

- Audio, visual, and smell effects will be turned off or reduced.
- Lighting levels will be adjusted.
- Capacity will be reduced.
- Dedicated sensory room.

These sessions will vary throughout the year with some happening on weekends and some
during weekdays in school holidays. Some will be mornings and some afternoons.

**Upcoming dates:** Sunday 17th October 10am-5pm. Sunday 31st January 10am-5pm.

Visual and sensory guides are available to download: Visual Story, Visual Timetable,
Sensory Information Guide, Sounds & Smells Guide and Mannequin Map.

events.title: Greipur Hjaltason – The Icebreaker UK Tour
events.raw:
**COMEDY: GREIPUR HJALTASON – THE ICEBREAKER UK TOUR** —
Oct 20, 8:00 pm - 10:00 pm, Hen & Chicken Studio.
events.summary: Icelandic stand-up Greipur Hjaltason's first UK tour. The £30 here is the Comedy Box's early-bird price; its own listing tops out at £35.
events.description:
Greipur Hjaltason — Iceland’s Comedian of the Year 2020 (yes, the competition wasn’t exactly fierce up north 😏) — has rapidly become one of the most recognisable voices in European stand-up comedy. Now, for the very first time, he’s taking his unique brand of humour on tour across the UK , ready to meet the people who helped propel him to international fame.

With over 2 million followers on Instagram, more than 800,000 fans on TikTok, and 1+ billion views, Greipur has taken the internet by storm. His rise began with viral videos featuring his razor-sharp wit, perfectly deadpan delivery, and brutally honest observations on parenting, relationships, and life on a tiny island full of volcanoes, glaciers, and questionable weather choices.

Online he’s known simply as @greipjokes — a comic voice that travels far beyond Iceland. His material leaps from everyday quirks to cultural weirdness, with a twist of Icelandic charm. One moment he’s lecturing about elves, the next he’s dismantling Nordic stoicism — and audiences everywhere crack.

Fresh off his digital domination and a guest spot on the award-winning Comedy Roundtable podcast, Greipur now steps off the screen and onto real stages across the UK. Expect sharp storytelling, sneaky sarcasm, and a mischievously charming presence that’s even better in person.

**From volcanoes and glaciers… to audiences across the UK. Greipur Hjaltason — live, unfiltered, and funnier than ever.**

events.title: Phil Melanson introduces Florenzer
events.timesText: Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.
events.raw: **Event 22/10: Phil Melanson introduces Florenzer** — From £6.00.
events.summary: Phil Melanson on his debut Florenzer, a queer historical novel set in fifteenth-century Florence.
events.description:
**Join us for a fantastic evening with Phil Melanson to discuss his brilliant debut, *Florenzer:* a queer, historical novel that paints a richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.**

**Date:**
Thursday 22nd of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£14.99 ticket with *Florenzer* (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***Florenzer***

*THE DAZZLING NEW HISTORICAL FICTION NOVEL FOR FANS OF THE SONG OF ACHILLES AND MARRIAGE PORTRAIT.*

15th-century Florence: where the river runs red with slaughterhouse blood and bronze statues glow in every square. Into its fold comes a young Leonardo da Vinci. Wayward and dreamy, he is different from the other artists' apprentices, drawn to what passes behind veils of steam in the baths and along the moonlit banks of the Arno.

Such habits have long belonged to Florence, but they carry risk in a city where anonymous accusations slipped into letterboxes destroy reputations overnight. Alongside Leonardo, two men pursue their own forms of immortality: Francesco Salviati, a priest willing to endure any degradation in the name of salvation, and Lorenzo de' Medici, heir to a great banking fortune, for whom wealth proves a shifting, uncertain thing.

Weaving together these three lives, *Florenzer* is a sensuous and richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.

*'The rift between Rome and Florence brings Melanson's three characters together in a bloody, vivid climax. All three characters are superbly drawn and Renaissance Florence leaps from the page...A stunning debut.' - The Times*

*'A captivating portrait of an all-too-human genius - subtle, erudite and exquisitely sexy.' - James Cahill, author of The Violet Hour*

*'Florenzer is a heady, intoxicating debut that examines the meaning of art in a time of turmoil. Melanson draws subtle, intimate portraits of his three protagonists, each of them caught between the worldly and the divine. Tortured Leonardo, ambitious Lorenzo and fanatical Salviati: the lives of these men intersect in surprising and sometimes bloody ways in the cutthroat world of Renaissance Italy. Told in rich, vivid prose, passion and desire permeate every page.' - Danielle Giles, author of Mere*

*'Introduces us to a teenage Leonardo still struggling to find himself amid the roiling artistic and political atmosphere of late-15th-century Florence... For a young man sexually attracted to other young men, this can be particularly dangerous...Yet his work may be his salvation.' - New York Times Book Review*

*'Impressively ambitious. . . An enjoyably sticky web of intrigue is spun, with much gossiping, bribing and backstabbing, and much shifting of allegiance between the great centres of power on the peninsula.' - TLS*

***ABOUT THE AUTHOR***

**Phil Melanson** is the author of the queer historical novel *Florenzer*, which was a National Bestseller, long-listed for the Centre for Fiction’s First Novel Prize, and an Allstora “(Very) Gay Book Club” Selection. He is a graduate of NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts and the University of Warwick, and in another life was a digital marketer for Hollywood film studios, working on campaigns for movies such as *Little Women, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again *and* Once Upon on a Time… in Hollywood*. He teaches with Boston University in London, where he lives with his husband.

events.description:
We're excited to welcome bestselling author Lucy Clarke to Bristol!

High on the cliffs of Morocco, far from the city lights and the souks,
stands The Surf House: a sanctuary for travellers chasing sunshine and
waves. But the idyll hides a dark mystery.

And when Bea washes in, seeking refuge after a dangerous encounter in
Marrakesh, she soon gets caught in the current.

A woman her age — who stayed in the same area, walked the same beaches, met
the same guests — disappeared one year earlier, vanishing without trace.

Somewhere inside The Surf House lies the truth, but there'll be a price for
uncovering it...

Join us for a special event with Lucy in conversation with Molly from the
Bristol Girls Surf Club!

Lucy Clarke is a Sunday Times bestselling author whose novels have sold over
a million copies worldwide. Her book *The Castaways* was a Waterstones
Thriller of the Month selection. When not on research trips, Lucy can be
found writing her destination thrillers from a beach hut on the south coast
of England.

events.summary: The Bungei Prize-winning Japanese novelist and their translator Polly Barton on bringing a 2004 debut into English, in collaboration with the Japan Foundation.
events.description:
We are delighted to be hosting a conversation between multi-award-winning
author Nao-Cola Yamazaki and literary translator Polly Barton! They will be
joining us in person to discuss Polly's translation of Nao-Cola's novella
*Don't Laugh At Other People's Sex Lives*.

First published in Japan in 2004, it's the book that launched Yamazaki's
career, earning them the 41st Bungei Prize and a movie adaptation. It's now
finally available in this deft English translation, and we can't wait to
hear more about the process of bringing it to new readers after all these
years.

Pre-order your copy (rrp £9.99) for a special discounted price with your
ticket, then collect on the night!

This event is presented in collaboration with the Japan Foundation.

**About the book.** A love story that feels both new and achingly true,
capturing the intensity, uncertainties and intimacy of falling for someone.
Art student Isogai first models for one of his tutors, the much older Yuri,
then begins a passionate affair with her. As he gets to know her better, he
struggles to understand his own emotions and his place in the world, just as
he yearns to be closer to her and for her to share more of herself with him.
A smash-hit in Japan, selling over 250,000 copies.

**About Polly Barton.** A writer and literary translator from the Japanese
whose translations include *Butter* by Asako Yuzuki, *Hunchback* by Saou
Ichikawa and *Where the Wild Ladies Are* by Aoko Matsuda. Her debut novel,
*What Am I, A Deer?*, was published in 2026.

events.summary: Matt Stellingwerf headlines, drawing on criminology, anthropology and being a New Zealander in Britain.
events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly flagship comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online

## Stand Up For The Weekend with Matt Stellingwerf featuring Milo Edwards plus compere Tom Glover

#### Headliner: MATT STELLINGWERF

Hamilton-Born New Zealander and Wangnui-raised farmer’s son, trained criminologist and stand up comedian…Matt Stellingwerf is a man of contradictions.

He expertly brings these contradictions to the stage with his typical low-key style and confidence finding the humour in topics as diverse as love, politics and a crazy interview he once conducted with a serial killer in Death Row!

Highly regarded by his peers, Matt Stellingwerf has won four NZ Comedy Guild Awards, including Best Newcomer. He is now UK based and respected nationwide by promoters and comedy venues.

A renowned MC and compere, Matt is a 3-time nominee for Best MC in New Zealand. Matt was a 2015 and 2016 nominee for the prestigious Billy T Award.

When this erudite satire-superstar gets onto the stage, the acceleration from zero to a hundred jokes is measured in seconds. Matt Stellingwerf’s deftly crafted jokes display a man full of seriously good comedic talent.

#### “*Stellingwerf’s comedy is intelligent, clever and thoroughly researched..all of the while being really likeable*” Libel

#### “…*an intellectual ‘Fonze’..extremely laid back and relaxed with the audience, seamlessly having banter and keeping his cool*” Keeping Up With NZ

[Matt Stellingwerf](https://www.mattstellingwerf.com/)

events.summary: Two hours with Concorde after closing, in three rotating groups — under the aircraft, inside the forward cabin and flight deck, then the simulator. Thirty-three places only.
events.description:
Hear about what it was like to fly faster than the speed of sound at 60,000 ft on a
technical tour of Concorde Alpha Foxtrot by former employees of BAC Filton & Weybridge, as
well as former Concorde at Filton guides. Perfect for the Concorde aficionado or those who
want to know more about the iconic supersonic passenger jet.

Enjoy a thrilling two-hour journey, beginning with a refreshing welcome drink upon
arrival. You will be divided into groups each rotating through three sections:

- **Underneath Concorde:** Discover the technical feats of the aircraft, highlighting its
  engineering innovations.
- **Onboard Concorde:** Explore the forward cabin and the flight deck, with a unique photo
  opportunity.
- **Concorde Flight Deck Simulator:** Experience the mock flight deck and delve into
  Concorde’s history through the exhibition.

To commemorate this unforgettable adventure, each guest will receive a personalised
certificate signed by a Concorde VIP. There are just 33 spaces for the exclusive tour.

events.description:
Join us for autumn fun, stories and exploration!

Perfect for families with children aged 0-9, this enchanting event will immerse you in the
richness and warmth of the season, celebrating nature this autumn.

Peep into our tiny world autumn doors and spot the fairies and animals that live behind
them. What stories do they tell? Let your creativity flow and create your own story/poem
inspired by our autumn creatures to take home with you.

This event is a delightful way to introduce young ones to the magic of the season with lots
of creative activities.

**What’s on:** story time with our friendly volunteers; face painting by our art students —
will you transform into a bat, a squirrel, or be decorated with leaves and acorns?; a drink
and a tasty treat on our terrace; spot the cuddly woodland birds and their friends hiding
in our museum; come dressed in your favourite costumes; make a paper woodland friend to
take home; and a nature walk with a special outdoor trail around the park and grounds.

October, Saturday 31 October, Sunday 1 November.

occurrence.pattern: Saturday 24 October, Sunday 25 October, Thursday 29 October, Friday 30 October, Saturday 31 October, Sunday 1 November

price.text: Entry tickets £5 per person; children under 4 free; discounted family group tickets available. Activities included in entry price.

events.raw:
24 October—1 November 2026

FAMILIES: These spooky activity days will investigate the past at The Red Lodge Museum
with something to do for all the family.
events.summary: Half-term in a dimly lit Tudor house: former residents in costume tell their own stories, tiny doors hide ghosts to find, plus crafts, face painting and a drink in the knot garden.
events.description:
Step into history this Halloween at The Red Lodge for a week of stories and exploration!

This enchanting event will immerse you in the rich history of one of Bristol’s most
intriguing historical houses, where the past comes alive.

Peep into our tiny world spooky doors and spot the ghosts and ghouls that live behind
them, can you find them all? What Spooky stories do they tell? Let your creativity flow
and create your own story or poem inspired by our spooky creatures to take home with you.

As you wander through the dimly lit halls, you’ll encounter former residents who will
guide you on a journey through time, sharing tales of the lives and the history of the
house. You can find out all about:

- Sir John Young, an Elizabethan gentleman, the first owner of the Red Lodge and host to
  Queen Elizabeth I
- Annie Woolham, a young Victorian girl and early resident of the Red Lodge Reform School
- Mary Henley, a Georgian lady who modernised the Red Lodge and turned it into a home

**What’s on:** story time with our volunteers during the year of reading; a creative
activity — make a God's Eye to ward off unfriendly spirits, a spooky paper pal, or
decorations to take home; spooky face and body painting; historical costume to dress up
in; and a drink and a tasty treat in our Tudor Knot garden.

**Happening on:** Saturday 24 October, Sunday 25 October, Thursday 29 October, Friday 30
October, Saturday 31 October, Sunday 1 November.

**Book tickets.** Entry tickets are £5 per person (except children under 4). Activities are
included in entry price. Discounted family group tickets available.

events.description:
Join us in the shop for a very special book signing with the one and only
Oliver Jeffers!

Oliver will be joining us to celebrate not only the release of his new
picture book *A Day Off School* (written by Oliver and illustrated by Kevin
Waldron), but also the new paperback edition of his classic *There's a Ghost
in This House*.

You'll get a free art print with every purchase of either of those two
books, and we'll also have an array of Oliver's incredible backlist on sale
too, ready for him to sign just for you.

Here's the lowdown on how it'll work on the day:

- You must purchase a £5 ticket to attend: this can be redeemed against any
  Oliver Jeffers book on the day (we'll have a large selection of his books
  available as well as the new ones!)
- One ticket required per group (up to 5 people)
- The signing will begin at 3:30pm and tickets are limited to ensure
  everyone will have time to get their books signed, but please be aware
  that you will have to queue!

events.title: An evening with Oliver Jeffers

price.text: £12.00; ticket types are event ticket only, or event ticket plus a copy of The Cave Downwind of the Cafe

events.raw:
**An evening with Oliver Jeffers**

Monday 26th October 2026, 7pm

The Planetarium @ We The Curious, 1 Millennium Square, Anchor Rd, Bristol,
BS1 5DB

£12.00
events.summary: A career-spanning conversation with the artist and picture-book maker, staged inside the We The Curious planetarium — the second of his two Storysmith dates that day.
events.description:
We are thrilled to welcome Oliver Jeffers back to Bristol for a very special
in-conversation event, and we've gone and hired an actual Planetarium for
the occasion!

This will be a fascinating, career-spanning chat that takes you right into
the world of one of our most beloved creatives. Fine artist, storyteller,
children's book creator, international force for good and ghost expert: we
are so excited to have Oliver back with us, and anyone who was with us back
in 2023 at the RWA will know that we're in for a mind-expanding time.

Tickets are on sale now!

**About Oliver Jeffers.** Oliver Jeffers' career in children's books began
with his highly acclaimed debut, *How to Catch a Star*, first published in
2004. Since then, he has become a worldwide phenomenon with book
translations in forty-nine languages. He has exhibited at the Brooklyn
Museum, the National Portrait Gallery in London and the Isabella Stewart
Gardner Museum. In 2022 he received an MBE for his Services in Art, and in
2026 joined Smartphone Free Childhood as their ambassador.

Access info can be found on the We the Curious website.

events.title: WOOFYT: Explore the Science of Music

price.text: Workshop places are free but must be booked in advance.

events.raw:
**Build, Play and Discover: The Science of the Organ. Featuring WOOFYT.**

Ever wondered how an organ creates its powerful sound?

Join us for a hands-on family experience exploring the science, technology
and creativity behind one of the world's most remarkable musical
instruments. Through WOOFYT, the Wooden One-Octave Organ for Young
Technologists, children and families can investigate how organ pipes work,
discover the mechanics behind music, and experiment with sound for
themselves.

Designed for curious minds of all ages, this interactive activity combines
music, engineering and discovery in a fun and accessible way.

Alongside the workshop, families can also enjoy [Crafty
Cathedral](https://bristol-cathedral.co.uk/whats-on/), with free drop-in
musical arts and crafts activities running throughout the morning. No
booking is needed for the craft activities.

Workshop sessions (75 minutes): 9.30am / 10.50am / 1.00pm / 2.20pm

Workshop places are free but must be booked in advance.

Part of [The Grand Organ
Festival](https://bristol-cathedral.co.uk/whats-on/the-grand-organ-festival/),
celebrating the return of Bristol Cathedral's organ following its major
restoration.

Wed 28 Oct | 9:30 - 15:30
events.summary:
Half-term family workshop built around WOOFYT, a wooden one-octave organ
children can take apart and play, to work out how pipes make sound. Four
free 75-minute sessions through the day, booked in advance, with drop-in
craft running alongside.

events.description:
**WOODWORKING HAND TOOL SHARPENING AND SET UP**

On this one day course you will learn how to sharpen and maintain
your chisels, planes and scrapers so that they are effective and are
a pleasure to use. We will cover all the essential sharpening know
how and then give you the opportunity to put it into practice under
our guidance.

You will also learn how to set hand planes and make fine adjustments
to get the best performance from them. Gain the confidence to get
your home workshop chisels and planes into shape!

**LEARN ABOUT:**

- Angles, bevels and shapes
- Sharpening stones and other abrasives
- Honing fluids
- Freehand sharpening and honing guides
- How to create a turned edge
- Hand plane tuning and set up

**COURSE LENGTH & TIMES:** 1 Day (Wednesday 10.30am – 3.30pm)

**SKILL LEVEL:** Suitable for everyone

**COURSE FEE:** £65.00

**INCLUDED IN THE COURSE FEE:** All materials, tutoring and tool use
– there are no additional costs.

Please bring along a woodwork chisel and/or plane from home to
practice on. If you don't have any to bring, just let us know and we
will make sure there is something available in the workshop for you to
use.

**CANCELLATION SPACES:** We run waiting lists for cancellation spaces
on all of our fully booked courses – to be added to a waiting list
please email hello@themakershed.co.uk.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Chloe Petts & Guests Featuring Jonny Pelham plus compere Jack Campbell

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

#### Headliner: CHLOE PETTS

Chloe Petts is one of the sharpest, funniest voices on the UK comedy circuit. Armed with razor-sharp observations, effortless charisma and an infectious warmth, they transform everyday life into brilliantly crafted stand-up. Whether they’re dissecting sport, politics, relationships or the glorious absurdities of modern Britain, Chloe’s quick wit and playful confidence keep audiences hooked from start to finish. A regular on television, radio and some of the country’s biggest comedy stages, they’ve earned acclaim for their intelligent, fearless and gloriously entertaining performances. Smart, energetic and laugh-out-loud funny, Chloe Petts is a comedian not to be missed.

Chloe Pett’s most recent show Big Naturals premiered at the Edinburgh Fringe in August 2025, and achieved a sell out run, with multiple sold out extra shows being added across the month. Chloe’s previous show, How You See Me, How You Don’t, came to the Fringe in 2024. The show was lauded with multiple four- and five-star reviews, with the Evening Standard telling audiences “Don’t mess with Petts and don’t miss [them] either”.

On television and radio, Chloe has appeared on Have I Got News For You (BBC 1) three times across 2024 and 2025, as well as Live at the Apollo (BBC) in 2025 and Bake Off: An Extra Slice (Channel 4), and hosted their own segment every Saturday morning on Sky Sports News.

#### “*Smart, insightful, hilarious, and completely relatable.*” Diva Magazine

#### “*One of the most compelling young comics*” The Guardian

#### “*Clearly a rising star whose name will soon be in lights*” London Evening Standard

#### “*World-class stand-up skills… drenched in laughs and warmth. We must never take Chloe Petts for granted.*” The Scotsman

Discover Chloe Petts here: [https://www.chloepetts.org/](https://www.chloepetts.org/)

events.description:
Yoga Foundations Workshop — Breath, Meditation, Posture & Balance

This Yoga Foundations workshop offers time and space to explore yoga
from the ground up.

We'll work with the four core parts of yoga — Breath, Meditation,
Asana (postures) and basic Philosophy — with a particular focus on
standing postures and balance, including Warrior I, II, III & IV, and
a small number of balance poses.

We'll take our time and work carefully, starting with the basics:

- where to place your feet
- how to breathe within the postures
- how the body organises itself to stand and balance

Alongside the physical learning, we'll explore the essence of these
postures — "what do you stand up for?" "What do you show up for?"

With 2.5 hours together (10:00–12:30), there is space to explore,
explain, rest & repeat – so learning has time to settle and
integrate.

The workshop finishes with Chinese tea for contemplation and light
snacks, offering a gentle close to the morning.

**Make a day of it?** Stay on site for brunch at the excellent
Cibomatto Italian Canteen, book in advance for the sauna and cold
plunge, or head out for a walk in the beautiful Nightingale Valley or
along the river towards Crews Hole.

**Why St Anne's House?**

- Free on-site parking (including accessible spaces)
- Accessible ground-floor Mill Room with step-free access
- Bristol Community Sauna & Cold Plunge on site for post-class
  relaxation
- A vibrant community hub with creative studios, café, and local
  projects

**What to Bring** — Wear comfortable clothes you can move in. Bring
your own yoga mat and props if you have them, plus a blanket and
pillow for relaxation. Mats are available to borrow if needed.

We’re bringing you Bristol’s biggest silent disco ever across two of the city’s most

biggest Silent Disco provider, Silent Disco King, and Propaganda.

events.description:
**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In September, we'll be delving into *Dream Count by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie*, a Sunday Times Bestseller that was also Longlisted for the Women's Prize for Fiction. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 4th of November

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *Dream Count***

**THE INSTANT SUNDAY TIMES NO.1 BESTSELLER; LONGLISTED FOR THE WOMEN'S PRIZE FOR FICTION**

*'Magnificent' SUNDAY TIMES*

*‘Extraordinary’ NEW STATESMAN*

*'The return of a literary titan' TELEGRAPH*

A searing, exquisite novel by the bestselling and award-winning author of Americanah and We Should All Be Feminists – the story of four women and their loves, longings and desires.

Chiamaka is a Nigerian travel writer living in America. Alone in the midst of the pandemic, she recalls her past lovers and grapples with her choices and regrets. Zikora, her best friend, has been successful at everything until – betrayed and brokenhearted – she must turn to the person she thought she needed least. Chiamaka’s bold, outspoken cousin Omelogor is a financial powerhouse in Nigeria who begins to question how well she knows herself. And Kadiatou, Chiamaka’s housekeeper, is proudly raising her daughter in America – but faces an unthinkable hardship that threatens all she has worked to achieve.

Dream Count is Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie’s searing, unforgettable story of these four women – a sparkling, transcendent novel that takes up the very nature of love itself.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: GARRETT MILLERICK

Garrett Millerick is an acclaimed stand up comedian, writer and director. His unique and versatile style has led to him being in great demand on the alternative and club circuits both in the UK and internationally.

Garrett is known for his grumpy, grouchy persona who is fed up with the pretenses of the modern world, aiming his criticism at everything from the fraudulent activity of the recycling industry to growing depression inflicted by miserablist, oversharing celebrities. His shouty, ironic delivery keeps you on the edge of your seat and the crushing punchlines can leave you exhilarated as he rages against yet more societal hypocrisies.

#### “*A virtuoso display of unforgivingly grumpy stand up delivered with fire in his soul*” Chortle

#### “*Stand up with an insolent twist*” The Sunday Times

#### “*Wonderfully funny*” The Times

#### “*Watching him let rip for one hour at an arts festival is a unique joy*.” The List

Discover Garrett Millerick here: [https://www.garrettmillerick.com/](https://www.garrettmillerick.com/)

events.title: Meet Cody Dahler!
events.raw:
**Meet Cody Dahler!**

Monday 9th November 2026, 13:00 - 15:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

Want to stop feeling like a thicky thicky dumb dumb in front of all your
mates?
events.summary: A lunchtime signing with the comedian and political satirist behind *The State of This!*, a plain-English guide to why British politics is the way it is.
events.description:
We are delighted to welcome writer and comedian Cody Dahler, signing copies
of his hilarious yet informative book, *The State of This!*

(The shop's own page says "welcome ... to Deansgate" here, which appears to
be copy carried over from another branch; the listing header and shop filter
both give Bristol - Galleries.)

Want to stop feeling like a thicky thicky dumb dumb in front of all your
mates?

Award-winning comedian, satirist, and political writer Cody Dahler launches
his blisteringly funny, sharply researched and pointedly accessible
deep-dive book, *The State of This!* at a time when UK politics feels more
like a never-ending circus of culture wars, personality clashes and
questionable decision-making. Cody uses his signature wit and razor-sharp
commentary to tackle the questions that leave people baffled, exhausted or
simply shouting at the telly: Why are people voting for Reform UK? Why did
we Brexit? What even is the House of Lords? Why are our rivers full of crap?
Are we at risk of becoming like the US? Why do our Prime Ministers keep
changing? And why, exactly, did outliving a lettuce become the benchmark for
political longevity?

*The State of This!* transforms complex political issues into something
readers can understand and laugh about. It is the perfect antidote to the
confusion, frustration and existential dread generated by the state of
Britain today.

Cody Dahler is an award-winning comedy creator, writer, and podcaster whose
sharp wit and unique voice have made him one of the most exciting talents
emerging from the UK comedy scene. He is the creator and host of The Truth
(In My Opinion) podcast.

events.summary: Comedian and podcaster Ali Woods headlines, on football, the environment and everything in between.
events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Ali Woods & Guests Featuring Harriet Dyer plus compere Adam Beardsmore

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ALI WOODS

Ali Woods is a half-English, half-Scottish comedian, podcaster and content creator. Ali is a refreshing mix of the ‘every man’ and the ‘modern man’, whose sensitivity and genuine interest in men’s mental health gives him a great perspective on the modern ‘lad’ culture which often features in his comedy. Ali is that wonderful blend of comedy with a heart, speaking on topics such as football, the environment, and many social causes close to his heart.

His online comedy sketches under the tag @aliwoodsgigs have gained millions of views and likes, and featured on LadBible and Buzzfeed UK. In 2022, he supported Russell Kane and Axel Blake on tour and in 2024 supported Adam Kay.

In 2024, Ali starred on Comedy Central Live and Stand Up Sketch Show. He also had a third sold out Edinburgh run with his show ‘At the Moment’ he then embarked on his first ever solo tour across the UK and Ireland to sold-out audiences, including a date at Bristol’s Hen & Chicken.

#### “*Ali Woods is a simply brilliant storyteller*” Everything Theatre

#### “*In a world of wannabes, Woods is the real deal.*” London Evening Standard

Discover Ali Woods here: [https://www.aliwoodsgigs.com/](https://www.aliwoodsgigs.com/)

events.title: The Dark Room with John Robertson
events.raw:
**Comedy: The Dark Room with John Robertson**

15 November · 20:00 – 22:00 · £17.50
events.summary: A live-action video game in its thirteenth year: John Robertson traps the audience in a dungeon, and they shout their way out. Sold out.
events.description:
Welcome to **THE DARK ROOM** – the legendary interactive comedy show that fuses improv, crowdwork and gaming to create an insane live-action videogame!

#### “*A Rocky Horror for nerds… reader, I howled*” Daily Telegraph

Now its 13th year, this high-octane interactive show is the brainchild of comedian & cult leader **John Robertson**. Filled with stand-up, appalling prizes and more audience chanting than you’d get at a protest – The Dark Room is a gut-busting rock n’ roll comedy experience for everyone who buys a ticket.

#### “*Will have you crying with laughter*”★★★★★ Broadway Baby

Permanently on tour The Dark Room has headlined stages at Glastonbury, PAX, Download Festival, MCM Comic Con, Utrecht International Comedy Festival 2000 Trees, UK Games Expo and Bluedot Festival, and sold out at Edinburgh Fringe, Soho Theatre and hundreds of theatres around the world.

Oh, and videos of The Dark Room roasting videogames and swearing at children keep popping up on people’s social media, which is nice.

Come watch, and if you want – play – the choose-your-own-adventure madness!

The crowd is trapped inside an inescapable dungeon with a sadistic videogame boss!

Pick increasingly surreal options off the screen and try to escape!

If you win – you get money!

If you fail – YA DIE! YA DIE! YA DIE!

Now, will you:

Find the Light Switch

Go North?

Abandon Hope?

Be sworn at by a man wearing spiked armour and a lot of leather?

(This option is permanently set to “On”)

**WINNER Chortle AwardRUNNER- UP NextUp Biggest Award in ComedyVIRAL AS HELL TikTok, Instagram SOLD OUT – Edinburgh Fringe 2019, 2022, 2023 & 2024**

#### “*NOT TO BE MISSED*” The Guardian
